papers.title: Linear Polarimetry of the Solar Corona during the Total Solar Eclipse of 8 April 2024: Multi-Band Observations and HDR Imaging
papers.summary: High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) multi-band linear polarimetry of the solar corona during total solar eclipses provides a vital ground-based diagnostic tool for mapping plasma morphology and magnetic topology in the inner and middle corona. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. Using a full-frame color CMOS detector paired with an 80~mm refractor, multi-band Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images were recorded simultaneously across three polarizer orientations ($-60^\circ$, $0^\circ$, and $+60^\circ$) using a 9-step exposure bracket ($1/800\text{~s}$ to $1/3\text{~s}$). We present an end-to-end data-reduction pipeline incorporating: (i)~a novel astrometric registration framework that reconstructs Sun-centric solar-disk coordinates via lunar-limb fitting, catalog star plate-solving, and ephemeris displacement calculations, achieving sub-pixel alignment; (ii)~a photometrically linear exposure-normalization HDR image synthesis; and (iii)~Multi-scale Gaussian Normalization (MGN) coupled with Polarization-to-RGB chromatic mapping. The resulting structurally enhanced polarization composites unravel a complex solar-maximum coronal topology characterized by helmet streamers and fine-scale striations traceable out to $\sim3\,R_\odot$. This framework establishes a high-resolution, photometrically calibrated dataset ready for subsequent polarized brightness ($pB$) and electron density inversions.

papers.title: Linear gas mass density: a unifying descriptor of Cosmic Filaments
papers.summary: Cosmic filaments connect the nodes of the large-scale web and are thought to harbour a substantial fraction of the low-z baryon budget, yet a physically motivated framework for organising their diverse gas properties has been lacking. Here we show that the linear mass density $\Lambda$ = M_gas/L_fil, measured within the entropy radius r_K (the peak of the radial gas entropy profile) plays this role, analogous to mass in halo physics. Using TNG300-1 at z=0, we characterise the structural, thermodynamic, and chemical properties of 5637 filaments spanning more than two decades in $\Lambda$. Filaments form a continuous thermodynamic sequence with $\Lambda$, ranging from long, thin, cool, metal-poor structures to shorter, wider, hotter, and more enriched ones, with core temperatures spanning two orders of magnitude across the full WHIM window. The ratio of mass- to volume-weighted temperature reveals a shift in heat distribution: low-$\Lambda$ filaments have their hotter gas preferentially associated with denser material, whereas in high-$\Lambda$ filaments the hotter gas is diffuse. Well-defined scaling relations connect $\Lambda$ to temperature, electron density, pressure, entropy, and metallicity, with the T-$\Lambda$ scaling qualitatively consistent with gravitational heating. We present the first measurement of the gaseous linear mass density function, revealing a broad distribution with a flat low-$\Lambda$ regime and a steep exponential decline at high $\Lambda$, analogous to the halo mass function. The integrated Compton-y parameter $Y^{\rm int}$ scales systematically with $\Lambda$, providing a tSZ proxy accessible to current surveys. Finally, galaxy richness per unit length correlates tightly with $\Lambda$ (Pearson r=0.80), enabling $\Lambda$-based classification of filaments from spectroscopic surveys alone and guiding targeted searches for the missing baryons in the cosmic web.

papers.title: The Central Molecular Zone of our Galaxy, a chemical complexity factory: first interstellar detections of molecules towards G+0.693
papers.summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of our Galaxy is a prime laboratory for interstellar chemistry because of its extreme conditions, such as shocks and high cosmic-ray ionisation rates. It is an efficient factory of molecules, with many species first discovered in CMZ sources. This document reviews key results from the study of the CMZ G+0.693-0.027 molecular cloud. Using ultra-sensitive broadband spectral surveys together with laboratory spectroscopy, more than 140 molecules have been identified, including 28 detected for the first time in the interstellar medium (ISM). These discoveries include prebiotic precursors of biomolecules, increasingly complex members of known molecular families, molecules containing periodic third-row elements (S, P, Na, Mg), high-energy stereo- and structural isomers, and new cations. Overall, these findings extend the known limits of interstellar chemical complexity and highlight the CMZ's potential to provide the molecular ingredients for prebiotic chemistry.

papers.title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. I. Evidence from Low-angular-momentum, High-$\alpha$ Stars Scattered Out of the Protodisk by Merger Events
papers.summary: Stars born in the high-$\alpha$ disk can later acquire low angular momentum through dynamical scattering during early merger events. Their age--metallicity distribution thus provides a fossil record of the history of both star formation and dynamical perturbations in the early Milky Way disk. Here we identify a sample of 2,078 such stars from more than two million Gaia DR3 subgiants with robust determinations of ages, kinematics, and abundances. From this sample we reconstruct their intrinsic age--metallicity distribution with a forward modeling approach. Our results confirm that these scattered stars are older and more metal-poor than the bulk of the high-$\alpha$ disk on average. In particular, the joint age--metallicity distribution reveals a robust two-component feature: a broad, dominant component with a peak age of $\sim$11.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.59$, and an older and more metal-poor component with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.86$. The presence of this two-component structure suggests that the high-$\alpha$ disk experienced episodic phases of star formation and chemical enrichment. The age distribution of the younger Splash component, compared with that of the high-$\alpha$ disk, provides evidence for a substantial dynamical perturbation at a lookback time of 10.8--11.5~Gyr, possibly associated with an early passage of Gaia--Sausage--Enceladus (GSE). The older Splash component, with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr, may preserve signatures of an earlier interaction, possibly associated with the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles (LKH) event.

papers.title: Star formation history of Draco revealed by DESI DR1: suppressed early star formation efficiency for Milky Way dwarf galaxies
papers.summary: Dwarf galaxies serve as fossils for understanding the early star formation history of the local Universe. In this work, we use stellar abundances for individual stars derived from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1) to investigate the star formation history of the dwarf spheroidal galaxy Draco. We simultaneously fit the stellar metallicity distribution function (MDF) and the [Mg/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend using the galactic chemical evolution (GCE) model flexCE. Our best-fit models imply a low star formation efficiency (SFE) of $0.003$ to $0.007\,\mathrm{Gyr}^{-1}$, which is about ten times lower than values reported in the literature, but consistent with recent SFE estimates for ultra-faint dwarf galaxies. By combining recent literature measurements, we find that the SFEs of Milky Way dwarf galaxies scale with stellar mass as $\mathrm{SFE}\propto M_\star^{0.24}$. A low star formation efficiency is associated with a strong outflow efficiency; we estimate a large wind mass-loading factor $\eta_{\mathrm{wind}}$ of approximately 172-260. This is well in line with the observed outflow-stellar mass relation and with the Feedback in Realistic Environment (FIRE) cosmological simulations. Our results demonstrate the power of large-scale, low-to-medium resolution stellar spectroscopic surveys to deliver robust constraints on the early formation history of galaxies in the local Universe.

papers.title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
papers.summary: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. We then compare each radio flux with the jet emission within an effective aperture set by the angular scale of the corresponding observation. The comparison across spatial scales favours a scenario in which the RIAF, rather than the jet, produces the compact $230~{\rm GHz}$ emission, while the jet dominates the lower-frequency radio, optical/UV and X-ray emission, but cannot produce the observed $\gamma$-rays. The RIAF connects the Bondi-scale gas supply to an accretion rate at the horizon of $1.1\times 10^{-5}$ of the Eddington rate, consistent with EHT polarimetry, and the two jets carry about a quarter of the accretion power, $1.2\times10^{43}~{\rm erg~s}^{-1}$ each. The framework presented in this work provides a simple way to disentangle the accretion-flow and jet contributions to the emission from nearby radio galaxies.

papers.title: Joint Fit of Galaxy Cluster Scaling Relations from Individual Weak Lensing Data: Comparison with Stacked Analysis and a Real Data Test
papers.summary: Stacking is the standard route to signal-to-noise in cluster weak lensing, but it destroys the cluster-by-cluster information that scaling-relation studies need. We instead fit every cluster's individual $\Delta\Sigma$ profile simultaneously, tying its mass and concentration to its own richness, redshift and magnitude gap, and compare with two stacked analyses of the same data: a forward-modelled stack sharing the same model and priors, and the standard two-step analysis. The magnitude gap (the BCG-to-brightest-satellite magnitude difference) enters the concentration, which the fossil-group picture ties to earlier assembly and more relaxed systems. On mock populations with triaxial haloes and miscentering, at DES Y3-like and LSST-like density, all three analyses recover the injected gap slope $\gamma_{\mathrm{cm}}$ with uncertainties that match the scatter between realisations, but not equally precisely: the joint fit scatters 1.2--1.3 times less than the forward-modelled stack, and 2 (DES-like) to 6.5 (LSST-like) times less than the two-step analysis, which is also biased in several other scaling-relation parameters. Applied to WaZP clusters with DES Y3 shears, the joint and forward-modelled fits agree on the gap coupling once the mass at fixed richness also depends on the gap, $\gamma_{\mathrm{cm}} = 0.065 \pm 0.033$ (forward-modelled) and$0.007^{+0.032}_{-0.033}$~mag$^{-1}$ (joint); the joint value is consistent with no coupling, so neither is a detection. The mass--concentration slope is consistent with zero in both, as expected from the upturn of the \citet{diemer2019} relation over this mass range. A gap coupling obtained in a model where the gap enters only the concentration need not survive a modest extension of that model.

papers.title: Exploring the Evidence for Evolving Dark Energy with the Jeffreys prior
papers.summary: We investigate the impact of applying the uninformative Jeffreys prior in a re-analysis of DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 CMB, and Type Ia Supernovae (DES-SN5YR, DES-Dovekie, Pantheon+, Union3). We incorporate this prior into new posterior inference and evidence calculations. We introduce novel techniques for interpreting the Jeffreys prior physically. To overcome the computational expense of the Jeffreys prior, we develop a fully $\texttt{JAX}$-based pipeline consisting of $\texttt{CosmoPower-JAX}$ emulators, gradient-based posterior inference using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), and evidence calculations using $\texttt{JAX}$-accelerated nested sampling. We demonstrate that while the parameter constraints on $w_0$ and $w_a$ remain robust to prior choice (exhibiting only minor shifts of the marginalised posterior towards the $\textit{Maximum A Posteriori}$ in less constraining dataset combinations), the Bayesian evidence is highly sensitive to the use of the Jeffreys prior; replacing uniform priors with the Jeffreys prior reverses the model-selection preference in dataset combinations that favour dynamical dark energy under the uniform prior, while strengthening existing preferences for $\Lambda$CDM. This is driven primarily by the significantly larger Occam penalty applied by the Jeffreys prior which penalises the overfitting of the data by a $w_0w_a$CDM model.

papers.title: PRISMS/U13151. A Glimpse into the Earliest Phases of Galaxy Formation through an Ultra-Faint System $\approx$ 500 Myr after the Big Bang
papers.summary: Detailed UV-to-optical studies of galaxies at z >= 10 have largely focused on bright systems (MUV <= -20 mag), leaving intrinsically faint galaxies virtually unexplored to date. Combining NIRCam, NIRSpec, and MIRI imaging and spectroscopy, we investigate UNCOVER-ABELL2744-13151 (U13151), an ultra-faint galaxy at z = 9.7995 (MUV = -17.44 mag), magnified by Abell 2744 ($\mu$ = 12.8). U13151 is very blue ($\beta$ ~ -2.64), ultra-low mass (log10(M*/Msun) ~ 6.68), young (~ 5.5 Myr), metal-poor (Z ~ 3-6% Zsun), and compact (Re ~ 122 pc). It exhibits negligible dust attenuation, extreme ionization conditions, and intense star formation (sSFR(Ha) ~ 94 Gyr-1, or equivalently M*/SFR(Ha) ~ 10.6 Myr). Despite similarities with much brighter galaxies, its low C/O, approximately solar Ne/O, and undetected nitrogen emission suggest enrichment dominated by core-collapse supernovae, in stark contrast with similar nitrogen-enhanced systems. U13151 might be undergoing its first major episode of star formation, assembling most (if not all) of its M* through five unresolved clumps. Its high ionizing photon production efficiency (log10($\xi_{\rm ion}$/ (Hz erg-1)) ~ 25.64) suggests, through a simple toy model, suggests, through a simple toy model, that similarly short-lived episodes could contribute significantly to the ionizing photon budget of low-mass galaxies during Cosmic Reionization. We explore different evolutionary scenarios, from U13151-like galaxies potentially representing the progenitors of Blue Monsters at higher redshifts to the possibility that such systems could be the early building blocks of present-day Milky Way-like galaxies. Our results highlight the fundamental role of MIRI in studying galaxies in the early Universe and the urgent need to investigate the faintest, lowest-mass systems to shed light on the fundamental physics driving the earliest phases of galaxy formation.

papers.title: Probing the Assembly of Triangulum: Precision Metallicities and $\alpha$ Abundances of M33's Star Clusters from APOGEE Integrated-Light Spectroscopy
papers.summary: The star cluster system of M33 provides an excellent opportunity to investigate whether galaxy formation physics is dependent on a galaxy's mass. Older globular clusters (GCs) trace hierarchical assembly and chemical enrichment, while younger clusters trace the recent star formation. By studying the M33 star cluster system as a whole, we can probe the formation physics of galaxies at a lower mass than the Milky Way, and look for signals of accretion. To that end, we present analysis of 37 M33 star clusters using high-resolution ($R\sim22,500$), near-infrared (1.5-1.7 $\mu$m), integrated light spectra from the APOGEE survey. We use full-spectrum fitting to obtain precision measurements of the clusters' kinematics, metallicities, and $\alpha$ abundances. We identify three populations of clusters from our measurements: young stellar clusters (~100 Myr) with broad Brackett absorption features; intermediate-age clusters (1-2 Gyr) that are metal-rich ([M/H]=-0.5 to +0.3) with roughly solar $\alpha$ abundance; and old (>5 Gyr), kinematically-hot and metal-poor GCs. These old GCs exhibit a broad range of kinematics (RV~-250 to -8 km s$^{-1}$), metallicities ([M/H]=-1.8 to -0.6) and $\alpha$ abundances ([$\alpha$/M]=+0.05 to +0.3), and we identify and discuss three GCs that show strong chemodynamical evidence of accretion into M33's halo. M33's GCs at [M/H]~-1.2 have a spread in [$\alpha$/M] of nearly 0.2 dex. This pattern is strikingly similar to the abundance distribution of Milky Way GCs, and indicates either that M33 and the Milky Way formed clusters similarly at early times, or that M33 hosts a significant population of accreted clusters in its halo.

papers.title: Extending the M33 Extinction Map with Radio and Far-Infrared Gas Observations
papers.summary: As the third-largest galaxy in the Local Group, M33 requires high-precision, wide-area extinction maps to recover the intrinsic luminosity and enable accurate studies, yet the available maps remain limited in coverage. In this work, we extend the stellar-based extinction map within the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury: Triangulum Extended Region (PHATTER) footprint to the outer disk by calibrating empirical $A_V$-H\,\textsc{i} and $A_V$-total hydrogen relations in the PHATTER overlap region. Within the PHATTER footprint, we retain the stellar-based map at 6$^{\prime\prime}$ resolution, and outside the area covered by the stellar-based extinction map we produce an extended map at $\approx 12^{\prime\prime}$ resolution. The resulting map preserves a continuous morphology across the PHATTER boundary and reveals clear spiral-arm and interarm contrast and patchy dust substructures across a broader area. The median and maximum extinction values, $\mathrm{median}(A_V)\approx 0.91$ mag and $A_{V,\mathrm{max}} \approx 2.62$ mag, are consistent with the high-extinction range reported by previous M33 studies, while naturally reflecting differences in tracers and spatial coverage. The extinction map provides a practical, publicly available dataset for galaxy-wide extinction correction and for further studies in M33.

papers.title: The EMA Justitia Probe: Terminator Frame-Based Deployment Orbit Selection and Surface Coverage Analysis
papers.summary: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) probe is designed to perform asteroid imaging during an uncontrolled ballistic descent to (269) Justitia. The mission design is constrained by main spacecraft proximity operations, uncertain asteroid gravity, limited knowledge of the final deployment trajectory, and requirements for illumination and safe operations. These constraints necessitate a mission design that ensures suitable illumination, attitude determination and control, and payload pointing throughout descent. The EMA probe concept of operations employs near-terminator deployment orbit geometry with continuous Sun visibility and two attitude control modes: single-axis Sun-spin for periodic imaging opportunities and three-axis asteroid-pointing for continuous asteroid visibility. Based on these modes, formal requirements are derived for deployment orbits that enable asteroid observations during ballistic descent. A deployment orbit selection method is developed using the terminator reference frame and a minimum boresight deviation margin. The method identifies families of orbit orientations satisfying illumination and payload observation constraints. Reference orbits are selected and verified through mission geometry analysis and trajectory propagation using a polyhedron gravity model. Asteroid surface coverage is then evaluated for uncontrolled tumbling, Sun-spin, and asteroid-pointing modes. The results characterize the expected imaging performance and demonstrate the feasibility of the EMA probe concept for close-proximity asteroid imaging. The proposed approach can also support future ballistic probe missions subject to similar operational and observational constraints.

papers.title: ERGO-ML and how to directly infer the multi-temperature nature of intra-cluster gas: simulation-based inference with TNG-Cluster
papers.summary: Though galaxy clusters are virialized and mostly in thermodynamic equilibrium, their internal gas thermodynamics are complex. The hot gas is multiphase and spatially inhomogeneous. The exact state of the gas contains important information about the internal physics governing clusters, however, measuring the multiphase distribution of the X-ray emitting gas is hard if not impossible with current observational methods. In this work (part of the ERGO-ML series), we present a direct inference method of the multiphase temperature distribution of the gas in the intra-cluster medium (ICM), applicable over a large range of spatial and mass scales. It works using different spectral resolutions (XRISM-like and Chandra-like) and realistic photon noise. Our method is an application of simulation-based inference. We train a neural-network on X-ray spectra in the range 0.1-10 keV, generated for $\approx 10^5$ sightlines of massive clusters ($M_{\rm 200c} = 10^{14.2-15.2}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$) from the TNG-Cluster cosmological MHD galaxy simulation. We show that our method recovers the mass-weighted temperature of both individual sightlines and entire clusters with an average prediction error of $< 0.01 ~\mathrm{dex}$, and the total gas mass within $0.04 ~\mathrm{dex}$. On top of that it gives accurate measures of the fraction of sub- and super-virial gas. Our method is capable of extracting the cooler gas phase even if the flux contribution is 3 orders of magnitude below that of the virial gas phase. We then show that we can accurately recover the spatial distribution of multi-phase gas both in relaxed and merging systems. This opens the way to studies of the multiphase nature of the ICM and the violent physics of feedback, accretion and merging.

papers.title: Evolving only the observed spacetime region: perfectly parallel lightcone simulations with sCOLA
papers.summary: Cosmological analyses of Stage-IV galaxy surveys require large ensembles of lightcone mock catalogues, but a full survey-scale $N$-body run costs of order $10^7$ CPU hours, putting such ensembles out of reach. We present a framework that produces survey-scale dark matter lightcones for a typical cost of order $10^3$ CPU hours each, based on the spatial COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (sCOLA) method. sCOLA decomposes an arbitrarily large volume into small tiles that are evolved independently, with buffer regions and non-periodic boundary conditions on the gravitational potential. We combine it with on-the-fly lightcone building, so that the evolved spacetime region reduces to the observed one: each tile is stopped as soon as the observer's past lightcone has left it, and only the tiles intersecting the region of interest are simulated at all. We further introduce two accuracy improvements to the sCOLA formalism: an LPT buffer that approximates the inflow of particles from outside the sCOLA box, and a second-order perturbative approximation to the gravitational potential at its boundaries; together they remove the large-scale inaccuracies of previous work and allow smaller tiles and buffers. Against a \texttt{Gadget4} reference in a $3.84\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Gpc}$ box with $3\,840^3$ particles, up to $k \simeq 0.4\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ the sCOLA lightcone reproduces the matter power spectrum to 1%, the velocity divergence power spectrum to 1.5% and the equilateral bispectrum to 2%, with no visible discontinuity at tile boundaries. The run cost $1\,300$ CPU hours, a factor of $2\,600$ below our $\texttt{Gadget4}$ run. Perfect parallelism at this cost brings ensembles of thousands of survey-scale lightcones within reach of a single allocation: $\sim 25\,000$ realisations of the $\textit{Euclid}$ Galactic north cap with a mass resolution of $10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ for $10^{7}$ CPU hours.

papers.title: Detection Forecasting for Blazars at MeV Energies with Fermi-LAT Swift-BAT Cross Match
papers.summary: Over the past two decades, the lack of an MeV $\gamma$-ray all-sky instrument has left an observational gap in blazar broadband emission. Recently, a new suite of MeV $\gamma$-ray instruments with sensitivity in the $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ range has been proposed, with the potential to far surpass the capabilities of previous all-sky MeV instruments. In this work, we forecast the capabilities of future MeV $\gamma$-ray instruments including COSI, GRAMS, newASTROGAM, and AMEGO-X to observe blazars. We pair total source count estimates of blazar luminosity functions with SED-modeled flux estimates of 76 blazars selected from a sample of 115 blazars cross-matched between the latest Fermi-LAT and Swift-BAT catalogs. We forecast that an instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-11}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect 61 of the 76 SED-modeled blazars, and expect a total population of a few tens to a few hundreds of Flat-Spectrum Radio Quasars (FSRQs), as well as a few hundred BL Lacs (BLLs). An instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect all 76 of the SED-modeled blazars, and we expect a total population of a few hundred to one thousand FSRQs and roughly one thousand BLLs. As MeV blazars have been observed to be extremely luminous and MeV $\gamma$-rays are minimally attenuated by the extragalactic background light, we use luminosity functions to estimate that blazars could be detected out to $z\approx6$. Lastly, we demonstrate detectability for blazars that have been proposed as neutrino-emitting candidates, as the MeV regime could provide a window into resolving lepto-hadronic degeneracies.

papers.title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
papers.summary: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.

papers.title: Deep X-ray Observations of the Gamma-ray Bright Pulsar Wind Nebula HESS J1303-631
papers.summary: HESS J1303$-$631 is an evolved, TeV-bright pulsar wind nebula (PWN) powered by the energetic radio pulsar PSR~J1301$-$6305, offset by $\approx7'$ northwest of the TeV centroid, with an energy-dependent gamma-ray morphology. We present new, deep joint Chandra (108 ks) and XMM-Newton (102 ks) observations of this field. High-resolution Chandra ACIS imaging resolves the pulsar from a neighboring point source that XMM-Newton cannot separate. The pulsar's 2-10 keV spectrum is well described by an absorbed power law with $\Gamma=2.02\pm1.04$ and an unabsorbed luminosity of $3.44\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $d=4.7$ kpc. Chandra also reveals faint diffuse emission east of the pulsar: a clumpy compact nebula on arcsecond scales ($\Gamma=2.98\pm0.53$, $L_X=4.15\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$) and a fainter extended nebula on arcminute scales ($\Gamma=1.20\pm1.25$, $L=4.36\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$). This morphology, the hard GeV counterpart, and the energy-dependent TeV emission together support an evolved, synchrotron-underluminous PWN whose X-ray nebula is far more compact than its TeV nebula. We also serendipitously discovered a transient X-ray source, CXOU~J130131.0$-$625919, in one of the nine new Chandra observations. Its hard spectrum ($\Gamma=1.4\pm0.3$) and 0.5-7\,keV luminosity of $3.34\times10^{32}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ at a fiducial distance of 3 kpc, together with a plausible near-infrared counterpart, most closely match a flare from a young pre-main-sequence star, though an active binary or compact-object binary is not excluded. Its large offset from HESS J1303$-$631 makes association with the TeV source unlikely.

papers.title: Cosmological implications of two mock TianQin standard siren catalogs generated under different background cosmological models
papers.summary: Space-borne gravitational wave (GW) detectors such as TianQin are expected to detect GW standard sirens for cosmological parameter estimation. All previous studies of TianQin adopted the $\Lambda$CDM model to generate mock standard siren data. In this work, we quantitatively investigate how the choice of background cosmological model affects mock TianQin standard siren (TQSS) catalogs and the corresponding cosmological implications. Adopting the $\Lambda$CDM model and a redshift-binned dark energy (DE) reconstruction model (the wbin model), we consider the bright standard sirens from massive black hole binary mergers and generate two mock TQSS catalogs, i.e. TQSS1 and TQSS2, respectively. We investigate the difference of the catalogs and further explore their cosmological implications within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) model, both individually and in combination with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, $\textit{Planck}$ 2018 cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, and DESY5 type Ia supernova (SN Ia) data. We find that there are only small differences between TQSS1 and TQSS2 catalogs, with a maximum relative difference of $1.48\%$ in the distance-redshift relation. In addition, either the TQSS1 or TQSS2 catalog alone gives cosmological constraints similar to those obtained from SN data, implying that these two catalogs can serve as a complement to mainstream cosmological observations. Most importantly, we find that both TQSS1+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 and TQSS2+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 are still expected to favor dynamical DE, with these two combinations showing a preference for dynamical DE at $2.3\sigma$ and $3.8\sigma$, respectively. Adopting different massive black hole seed models does not impact the cosmological implications of the mock TQSS catalogs. Our study indicates the importance of considering different cosmological models in the standard siren forecasts for DE.

papers.title: X-ray Comptonization in an Accreting Kerr Black Hole System with a Tilted Disc and Thermal Corona; A General-Relativistic Monte Carlo Simulation: I. Model, Radiative Transfer and Spectral-Timing Properties
papers.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the X-ray emission of accreting black hole binaries are commonly attributed to the relativistic Lense--Thirring precession of the inner accretion flow, in which a hot inner flow, tilted with respect to the black hole spin axis, precesses as a solid body while a cooler outer disc remains at its own, different tilt -- a warped, Bardeen--Petterson-type geometry. Testing this picture requires a radiative-transfer model that self-consistently follows photons through such a system: from emission near the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), through Compton scattering in a hot corona, to possible reflection off the misaligned outer disc, all under the full effects of light bending in Kerr spacetime. In this first paper of a two-part series, we present a general-relativistic Monte Carlo (GRMC) radiative-transfer model of a misaligned, warped, two-zone accretion system around a Kerr black hole. We describe the disc--corona geometry, the seed-photon prescription, the photon-transport engine -- including the geodesic integration scheme, the coronal Compton-scattering module and the outer-disc reflection treatment -- and the observer pipeline used to construct energy spectra, photon path-length and arrival-time distributions. We present the resulting energy spectra, light curves and spectral lags as functions of the black hole mass, corona size, outer-disc geometry, reflection albedo, photon-injection radius and observer inclination, and show how gravitational light bending systematically lengthens the path-length and arrival-time distributions of the escaping radiation. This model and its spectral-timing predictions form the foundation for Paper II, which extends the framework to track the full photon polarization state and presents the resulting energy- and precession-phase-resolved polarimetric signatures.

papers.title: Low-mass and High-sSFR H$\alpha$ Emitters at $z \sim 2$ in the ZFOURGE-COSMOS Field
papers.summary: We present a near-infrared spectroscopic follow-up study of seven H$\alpha$ emitter candidates at $z\sim2$ in the ZFOURGE-COSMOS field, selected via the $K_{\rm s}$-band flux excess method. Spectra obtained with Subaru/SWIMS confirm strong H$\alpha$ emission line at $z=2.06-2.49$ for all the targets. Three galaxies are low-mass systems ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot) 10$) on the star-forming main sequence. The low-mass galaxies show consistent H$\alpha$ flux measurements between the $K_{\rm s}$-band flux excess method and the spectroscopy, whereas the high-mass galaxies show higher H$\alpha$ flux inferred from the $K_{\rm s}$-band flux excess than the spectroscopic measurement which may be attributed to their extended star formation distributions. The low-mass galaxies exhibit extreme [O III] $\lambda5007$ emission with high rest-frame equivalent widths ($\mathrm{EW}_{\mathrm{rest}}$) ranging from 480 to 1064 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. They are characterized by high [O III]/H$\beta$ ratios ($>4$) and weak [O II] and [N II] emission lines, indicating high ionization parameters and low metallicity. The line ratios are comparable to those of star-forming galaxies at $z \gtrsim 6$ and their local analogs. JWST/NIRCam imaging reveals a clear mass-dependent color gradient: the low-mass galaxies present positive F115W-F277W radial gradients with blue cores, while the high-mass galaxies exhibit negative gradients with red cores. These results suggest distinct assembly pathways for low- and high-mass galaxies during the cosmic noon epoch.

papers.title: Energy extraction from a rotating black hole via magnetic reconnection: Bumblebee gravity
papers.summary: Many efforts were made in order to better understand the energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating black hole, following the work of Comisso and Asenjo in 2021. We also tried to make some progress in our previous works, in which we discussed differences between bulk plasma with different streamlines and also defined the covering factor as an internal property of an accretion system to quantify its capability on extracting energy via magnetic reconnection from its central black hole. In this study, we aim to explore this topic within the framework of a Kerr-Sen-like spacetime induced from Bumblebee gravity, which, among various alternative theories of gravity beyond pure Einstein gravity, stands out as a promising candidate for explaining certain high energy astrophysical phenomena. More specifically, we would like to analyze the influence of the rate of Lorentz symmetry breaking and the Bumblebee charge, the two additional parameters in Bumblebee gravity except for the black hole mass and spin, on the energy extraction via magnetic reconnection. By analyzing the allowed regions for energy extraction and the variations of covering factor, we find that energy extraction becomes more likely to succeed and tends to occur closer to the central region when the spacetime carries bigger rate of Lorentz symmetry breaking and Bumblebee charge. Furthermore, our results indicate that the most favorable spacetime configuration for energy extraction via magnetic reconnection, when the extractable energy of the central black hole is determined, corresponds to the scenario in which the cosmic censorship hypothesis is marginally not violated.

papers.title: Cislunar navigation is an observability problem: arc-length thresholds, Gramian conditioning, and the Doppler lever
papers.summary: Dilution of precision is the standard way to describe navigation geometry and it does not apply in cislunar space: its derivation presumes a snapshot solution in which simultaneous measurements determine the state at one instant. A spacecraft tracked by inter-satellite ranging in the Earth-Moon three-body problem has no such solution: range is a function of position only, so the velocity columns of the measurement Jacobian vanish identically and the state is unobservable however many links are in view. The correct figure of merit is dynamical, because the three-body flow carries velocity information into later range measurements. We demonstrate this on four differential-corrected planar distant retrograde orbits, reporting the observability Gramian rather than a dilution of precision. Instantaneous range-only geometry has rank 2 of 4; the full state becomes observable only after a tracking arc of 2.09 h, the first sampled arc at full rank on a 0.26 h grid, and a square-root information filter recomputing the same quantity by a different route becomes well-posed at exactly that arc. Beyond it, conditioning improves monotonically with arc length, the Gramian condition number falling from 1.2e11 at 3 h to 1.4e5 at 48 h. Adding range rate lifts the instantaneous rank from 2 to 4, so a Doppler-capable link makes a snapshot solution exist where a range-only link cannot. Lifting the known-reference assumption, the joint problem of estimating a station and the satellites' states and clocks together is rank-deficient by exactly one without an external interferometric observable in all twenty realizations tested, and full rank with it; the deficiency persists only to four satellites. For the configurations studied, cislunar navigation requirements are better written as arc-length, conditioning and measurement-type budgets than as dilution-of-precision thresholds, which are undefined here.

papers.title: Static tidal Love numbers of Schwarzschild and non-Schwarzschild black holes in quadratic gravity
papers.summary: We calculate the static electric quadrupolar response of black holes in four-dimensional quadratic gravity, with action $R-\alpha C^2+\beta R^2$. The Schwarzschild solution has zero massless gravitational Love number under the stated boundary conditions. A numerical non-Schwarzschild solution instead has a nonzero negative response. At $\alpha/r_h^2=1/2$, we find $\lambda_E/r_h^5\simeq-0.1224928$ and $k_2^{(r_h)}\simeq-0.1837391$, with a final outer-endpoint change in $k_2^{(r_h)}$ of about $1.60\times10^{-7}$. We explain how the background is obtained by shooting and how the tidal solution is selected by matching at an intermediate radius. The perturbations are written in Kodama--Ishibashi gauge-invariant variables. After the scalar-curvature perturbation is excluded by horizon regularity and the absence of an applied scalar tide, the remaining static sector has three coupled second-order radial equations. We define the curvature amplitudes in these equations and describe why simple attempts to separate them fail. The coupling scan shows a negative response approaching zero near the Schwarzschild intersection. We also explain why this full-theory result does not conflict with the removal of curvature-squared operators in a perturbative low-energy expansion.

papers.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
papers.summary: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

papers.title: Destinies of Plasmoids Formed from the Magnetic Reconnection Occurring within the Ergo Region of a Rotating Black Hole
papers.summary: It is widely accepted that magnetic reconnections occur successively in black hole accretion flows, especially on the equatorial plane, owing to the formation of the equatorial current sheet. When magnetic reconnection takes place within the ergosphere of a rotating black hole, one of the ejected plasmoids (denoted as $p_-$) may acquire negative energy-at-infinity density, while the companion plasmoid (denoted as $p_+$) correspondingly carries the energy extracted from the black hole. This mechanism, known as the Comisso-Asenjo process, provides a viable astrophysical pathway for extracting energy from a rotating black hole. Generally speaking, two conditions have to be satisfied for successful energy extraction. First, $p_-$ is generated via magnetic reconnection with negative energy-at-infinity density. Second, the associated $p_+$, which carries the extracted energy, must escape to infinity. Though a number of studies have promoted the theory of the Comisso-Asenjo process, the escape of $p_+$ lacks consideration. In this work, we adopt geodesic approach to systematically examine the destinies of $p_+$ after ejection, thereby establishing the complete conditions for energy extraction from a rotating black hole via magnetic reconnection. We redefine the covering factor, for which only escaping $p_+$ are counted. This quantity reflects how probable the successful energy extraction occurs in an accretion system. Through analysis of this revised covering factor, we identify a lower bound on the black hole spin, $a=0.8005$, below which energy extraction via magnetic reconnection can never succeed, no matter how high the magnetization of the bulk plasma is. This limit suggests that the spin-down of a black hole caused by successive magnetic reconnections would terminate once the spin decreases to approximately 0.8005.

papers.title: Moving Beyond Quasinormal Modes and Reinterpreting Direct Waves in Binary Black Hole Merger-Ringdowns
papers.summary: Based on black-hole perturbation-theory calculations and an effective-one-body picture of binary black hole mergers, it has been suggested that a direct wave may be present and measurable in the ringdown. Furthermore, it has been suggested that this signal might originate from substantially inside the light ring (or photon sphere) of the remnant black hole, perhaps even from close to the event horizon. In this paper, we present three independent strands of evidence against such claims. In the process, we show that there is indeed an early-time part of the ringdown signal that cannot be directly modeled by quasinormal modes. However, there is no evidence that this is a direct wave as it has previously been defined, and we show that the properties of this component are related to the remnant's light ring rather than its horizon.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
papers.summary: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.

papers.title: HyQ-LC: Improving Light-Curve Classification with Hybrid Quantum--Classical Learning
papers.summary: Light curves reveal stellar variability and support studies of stellar evolution and cosmic distances. Reliable classification is therefore important for large time-domain surveys. We present HyQ-LC for ten-class stellar light-curve classification using 359 handcrafted features and 633,034 training objects. The main model combines a window multilayer perceptron (MLP) backbone with a nine-qubit readout using amplitude encoding and angle re-uploading. Both this hybrid and its pure-MLP control have 44,238 parameters. On a shared 20,000-object test set, the hybrid has macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1) point gains of 0.8276 and 1.2393 percentage points over the pure MLP on two fine-tuning seeds. A separate fixed-fusion configuration achieves slightly higher Macro-F1 but lower accuracy than approximately budget-matched LightGBM. Its positive class-level differences are concentrated in CEP, RRC, and ROT, while the full-budget LightGBM reference scores higher on both metrics. All circuits are simulated classically. The comparisons retain existing validation-selected checkpoints and use the same test objects, with features, predictions, and recomputation code publicly available. The results identify point-estimate improvements over the tested controls while leaving the specific contribution of the quantum branch unresolved.

papers.title: Searching for lensed gravitational waves with unlensed templates
papers.summary: Gravitational lensing can split the signal of a binary merger into two images, which either overlap and interfere or arrive as separate events. We show that the matched-filter output of every two-image template can be straightforwardly constructed from the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) time series that searches already compute with unlensed templates. This enables a marginalized detection statistic that increases search sensitivity without additional matched filtering and is more than 150 times faster than an explicit lensed template bank. For overlapping images in the geometric-optics regime, our two-image method recovers $\gtrsim97\%$ of the optimal SNR from point-mass and singular isothermal lenses, compared with as little as $67\%$ captured by unlensed templates, with substantial gains also for Chang-Refsdal and cored isothermal lenses. Overlapping lensed signals moreover fail the signal-consistency test that is used to down-rank noise transients. Our two-image method restores the consistency and increases the sensitive volume by roughly $2$-$4\times$ for the strongly down-ranked signals. For separated images, our method enables an efficient coherent search for pairs in which neither image is significant alone. Near fold caustics, this increases the sensitive volume by factors of 1.8-2.6 over requiring two independent detections, and up to 1.6 over a targeted counterpart search. Our method is applicable to any matched-filtering search.

papers.title: The FENIKS Survey: Stellar-Halo Mass Relationship of Central and Satellite Galaxies in UDS and COSMOS at 0.2 < z < 4.5
papers.summary: We present the observed Stellar-to-Halo mass relationship (SHMR) spanning 0.2 $< z <$ 4.5 enabled through galaxy clustering and abundance measurements from two large (effective area $\sim$ 1.61 deg$^{2}$) and homogeneously prepared photometric catalogs $-$ UltraVISTA ultra-deep stripes DR3 (COSMOS) and FENIKS v2 (UDS). To translate these measurements into the SHMR, we introduce a novel halo occupation distribution (HOD) fitting approach (``smooth-$z$'') whereby HOD parameters between neighboring $z$-bins are disallowed sharp changes through continuity priors. As a result, the high constraining power at $z$ $\lesssim$ 2, due to a much wider dynamical range in stellar mass ($\sim$ 3 dex), helps constrain the SHMR at $z$ $\gtrsim$ 2, where that range shrinks down to $\lesssim$ 1 dex. We find a clear \textit{downsizing} trend in halo mass scale with peak integrated star-forming efficiency (SFE), M$_{h}^{peak}$ as it consistently decreases from 10$^{12.69^{+0.08}_{-0.08}}$ M$_{\odot}$ at z $\sim$ 4 to 10$^{12.17^{+0.03}_{-0.03}}$ M$_{\odot}$ at $z$ $\sim$ 0.35, exhibiting a decline of 0.52 dex. Furthermore, we show that if we had relied on COSMOS data alone (as opposed to UDS+COSMOS), as has been done by many preceding studies, M$_{h}^{peak}$ would be systematically lower by up to $\sim$ 0.2 dex at $z$ $<$ 1.25, highlighting the importance of mitigating cosmic variance. Finally, for the first time, we show how the integrated SFE evolves with redshift as halos grow in mass along their progenitor merger trees, instead of at fixed halo masses.

papers.title: Novel geometrical test of cosmological expansion from photometric data
papers.summary: Aim. In tomographic cosmic-shear observations, the Bernardeau, Nishimichi, Taruya (BNT) transform allows us to build weak lensing transformed maps for which the contribution from low-redshift lenses is nulled. As this transformation depends specifically on the expansion rate of the Universe and is independent of the matter distribution properties, it can be leveraged to extract information from large-scale structure probes at arbitrary non-linear scales. Thus, it provides constraints on cosmological background evolution. Methods. We demonstrate the applicability of the BNT transform as a probe by designing a null test and evaluating its performance for Stage IV weak lensing projects. Results. Using a Fisher matrix analysis combined with parameter sampling, we show that this approach can significantly enhance constraints on the dark energy equation of state. In such surveys, apart from photometric redshifts uncertainties, performance is expected to be limited primarily by shape noise, rather than cosmic variance, making substantial improvements possible thanks to better designed surveys in the future.

papers.title: Antenna Technology Readiness for the Black Hole Explorer (BHEX) Mission
papers.summary: The Black Hole Explorer (BHEX) will be the first sub-mm wavelength Space Very-Long-Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) mission. It targets astronomical imaging with the highest ever spatial resolution to enable detection of the predicted photon ring image feature of a supermassive black hole. BHEX is being proposed for launch in 2031 as a NASA Small Explorers mission. The BHEX science goals and the mission opportunity require a large, high precision, lightweight, spaceborne antenna. We present a survey of the technology landscape for realizing such an antenna. Technology readiness (TRL) for the antenna is discussed and assessed to be at TRL 5. A description of our technology maturation efforts towards TRL 6 is provided. Design studies leading to the preliminary design of a high efficiency antenna based on metallized carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) technology with a large 3.4 m primary reflector, a surface precision of < 40 {\mu}m to allow efficient operation up to 320 GHz, and a mass of only ~ 50 kg are outlined. Current plans anticipate attaining TRL 6 in 2027-28. Completed studies leading to the preliminary design point to a large margin in surface precision which also opens up applications at significantly higher THz frequencies, beyond BHEX.

papers.title: Supernova dust synthesis --- Carbonaceous dust in the very early universe
papers.summary: Recent observations have revealed the spectral feature of carbonaceous grains even in a very distant galaxy. We develop a state-of-the-art dust synthesis code by self-consistently solving molecule and dust formation in supernova (SN) ejecta that contain various elements in different layers. With a progenitor mass $25~M_{\odot}$ and explosion energy $10^{52}$ erg, we run the following four test calculations to investigate the impact of input physics. (i) With molecule formation solved, our SN model produces $8.45\times 10^{-2}~M_{\odot}$ carbonaceous grains. (ii) If all available C and Si were initially depleted into CO and SiO molecules, respectively, the C grain mass could be underestimated by $\sim 40\%$. In these two models producing $0.07~M_{\odot}$ $^{56}$Ni without mixing fallback, a large amount of silicates ($0.260~M_{\odot}$) created in O-rich layers are also ejected and likely to hide the spectral feature of carbonaceous grains. We then consider mixing-fallback that can reproduce the observed elemental abundance ratios of C-normal and C-enhanced extremely metal-poor stars in the Milky Way. (iii) In the former, the mass ratio of carbonaceous to silicate grains is still small ($\sim 0.3$). However, (iv) in the latter (known as a ``faint SN''), while the C grain mass is unchanged ($6.78\times 10^{-2}~M_{\odot}$), the silicate mass is reduced ($9.98\times 10^{-3}~M_{\odot}$). Therefore, we conclude that faint SNe can be a significant carbonaceous dust factory in the early Universe.

papers.title: Redshift Assessment Infrastructure Layers (RAIL): Rubin-era photometric redshift stress-testing and at-scale production
papers.summary: Virtually all extragalactic use cases of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) require the use of galaxy redshift information, yet the vast majority of its sample of tens of billions of galaxies will lack high-fidelity spectroscopic measurements thereof, instead relying on photometric redshifts (photo-$z$) subject to systematic imprecision and inaccuracy best encapsulated by photo-$z$ probability density functions (PDFs). We present the version 1 release of Redshift Assessment Infrastructure Layers (RAIL), an open source Python library for at-scale probabilistic photo-$z$ estimation, initiated by the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC) with contributions from the LSST Interdisciplinary Network for Collaboration and Computing (LINCC) Frameworks team. RAIL's three subpackages provide modular tools for end-to-end stress-testing, including a forward modeling suite to generate realistically complex photometry, a unified API for estimating per-galaxy and ensemble redshift PDFs by an extensible set of algorithms, and built-in metrics of both photo-$z$ PDFs and point estimates. RAIL serves as a flexible toolkit enabling the derivation and optimization of photo-$z$ data products at scale for a variety of science goals and is not specific to LSST data. We thus describe to the extragalactic science community, including and beyond Rubin the design and functionality of the RAIL software library so that any researcher may have access to its wide array of photo-$z$ characterization and assessment tools.

papers.title: Revisiting the CMB homogeneity scale: low multipoles removal effect and extragalactic foreground masking
papers.summary: The Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) reaches homogeneity at relatively modest angular scales compared to the expectation of the standard $\Lambda$CDM model revealing an important challenge to the theoretical predictions. We analyze this inconsistency through the homogeneity scale $H$ and the slope of the homogeneity index at $\theta = 90^\circ$. We find that the removal of low multipoles, in particular the quadrupole, from both the data and the $\Lambda$CDM synthetic CMB maps, significantly improve the consistency between models and observations. This adds to indications of the relevant contribution of the low value of the CMB quadrupole to the observed anomalies in the homogeneity scale. Due to the presence of a new extragalactic foreground in the CMB maps, we have performed statistical analyses with different masking taking into account the regions mostly affected. In particular we consider galaxies in the local neighborhood which are expected to affect more significantly the large angular scales. We find that by masking these regions, the analysis cannot solve the discrepancy between the observations and the $\Lambda$CDM model in spite of a small improvement of their mutual consistency. The studies with both foreground masking and low-$\ell$ removed CMB maps show similar results than those of the full CMB map indicating that the main discrepancy between theory and observations is associated to the quadrupole anomaly and may require more exhaustive analysis.

papers.title: Towards the Habitable Worlds Observatory: Retrieval of Reflection Spectra from Evolving Earth Analogues using 1D CNNs
papers.summary: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will characterize Earth-like exoplanets from low-resolution reflected-light spectra. To assess how atmospheric evolution shapes what can be recovered, we trained a convolutional neural network on 109,945 spectra generated with the Planetary Spectrum Generator for Archean, Proterozoic, and Modern atmospheres under LUVOIR-B and HabEx/SS observing assumptions, separating the contributions of observational noise and model variability. We find that recovery depends jointly on abundance and spectral structure. Across eras, O$_2$ recovery weakens in Proterozoic atmospheres and CH$_4$ becomes reliable only when abundant, while an isolated UV band yields robust Modern O$_3$ recovery ($R^2\simeq0.98$) despite poor Modern CH$_4$ recovery ($R^2=0.32$-$0.35$). Without being supplied feature locations, the network assigns $58$-$71\%$ of total attribution to visible wavelengths, while the ultraviolet remains decisive for O$_3$ and the near-infrared for CH$_4$ and CO$_2$. Aggregate retrieval leverage declines beyond approximately $1.7\,\mu$m, supporting a practical long-wavelength boundary in this setup. These wavelength dependencies also shape detectability. At baseline noise, $83$-$85\%$ of Modern O$_2$ cases satisfy a $3\sigma$ criterion, while Proterozoic O$_2$ remains below $50\%$ when noise is halved and Modern CH$_4$ remains below $3\sigma$ as observational noise approaches zero because model uncertainty caps its significance. Together, these results imply molecule-specific priorities for HWO trade studies. Low-abundance O$_2$ retains considerable leverage from improved observational quality while motivating better inference, whereas at the 1,000-hour benchmark O$_3$ and Modern CH$_4$ show predominantly model-associated uncertainty in these networks, motivating broader training coverage and improved uncertainty calibration.

papers.title: A High Incidence of Mid-infrared Variability in Local Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies
papers.summary: We explore mid-infrared (MIR) variability in local ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; infrared luminsoity $L_{\rm IR}>10^{12}\ L_\odot$) utilizing the $\sim$11 years of photometry from the NEOWISE multi-epoch catalog of {\it Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer} ({\it WISE}). We identify 30 variable ULIRGs with statistically significant MIR variability. The variability is observed on timescales of a few years, implying that the MIR-emitting regions are compact ($\lesssim 1$ pc). The difference between maximum and minimum $W2$ (4.6 ${\rm \mu}$m) band luminosity ($\Delta L_{\rm W2}$) of the 30 variable ULIRGs range from $\Delta L_{W2}$ = $7\times10^{42}$ to $5\times 10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The $\Delta L_{W2}$ of 25 variable ULIRGs out of 30 are greater than $\Delta L_{W2}$ = $1\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, surpassing the MIR luminosity {range} observed in known supernovae (SNe; $L_{\rm 3.6\ {\rm \mu m}}$ and $L_{\rm 4.5\ {\rm \mu m}}$ < 10$^{42.3}$ erg s$^{-1}$). Therefore, the MIR variabilities in these 25 ULIRGs are most likely driven by tidal disruption events (TDEs) or intrinsic changes in their active galactic nuclei (AGN) torus emission. Our sample includes hard X-ray detected AGNs (e.g., UGC 05101) and previously reported TDE candidates (IRAS F01004-2237, IRAS 05189-2524). All 25 also exhibit at least one AGN signature(s) besides the MIR variability, suggesting that even if the MIR variability originates from TDEs, the black holes responsible are likely AGNs. Our results suggest that MIR variability is an effective tool for detecting buried AGNs and highlights the intense nuclear activity in ULIRGs.

papers.title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass-Radius-Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
papers.summary: We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass-radius space instead of pressure-energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass-radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass-radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass-radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

papers.title: The MAGPI Survey: co-evolution of baryons and dark matter in star-forming disk-like galaxies at $0.1 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.85$
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of the dark matter (DM) content and its structural dependence in star-forming disk-like galaxies at intermediate redshifts ($0.1 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.85$), utilizing spatially resolved kinematic data from the MAGPI survey. We report the following: (1) Low stellar mass galaxies ($M_{\rm star} 10^{10.5}\, M_\odot$) systems exhibit relatively low DM fractions in their inner regions ($\langle f_{_{\rm DM}} \rangle \sim 0.47$) which is equivalent to local massive disk galaxies (e.g., Milky Way and Andromeda). This suggests a mass-dependent structural dichotomy, most-likely governed by a combination of internal galactic processes and environmental influences. (2) A tight inverse correlation between $f_{_{\rm DM}}$ and baryon mass surface density ($\Sigma_{\rm bar}$), with intrinsic scatter of $\sim 0.11$ dex. This is consistent with an inside-out baryon assembly scenario and suggests that the fundamental structural correlations of galaxies were already established by $z\sim 0.85$. (3) No significant evolution in $f_{_{\rm DM}}$ with redshift across the MAGPI window, and when combined with higher-redshift ($0.6 \leq z \leq 1.5$) data from Sharma et al. 2025, we quantitatively show that the reported decline in $f_{_{\rm DM}}(z)$ is most-likely due to observational biases against low-mass systems at $z > 1$. These results offer empirical evidence for a scenario in which disk-like galaxies evolve through a co-regulated build-up of baryonic and DM components, preserving internal structural regularities (such as the total mass distribution and rotation-curve shape) throughout cosmic time.

papers.title: Effects of Viscosity on Sloshing Cold Fronts in Galaxy Clusters
papers.summary: The viscous properties of the intracluster medium (ICM) remain poorly constrained. Cold fronts-sharp discontinuities formed during cluster mergers-offer a potential avenue to probe the effective viscosity of the ICM. Velocity shear across these fronts should generate Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities (KHI), unless viscosity or magnetic tension suppresses them. We perform cluster merger simulations incorporating four ICM viscosity models: (A) inviscid, (B) isotropic Spitzer viscosity, (C) anisotropic Braginskii viscosity, and (D) Braginskii viscosity limited by microinstabilities. The isotropic Spitzer viscosity (case B) strongly suppresses KHI, producing smooth cold front surfaces, while the inviscid (A) and microinstability-limited (D) cases show prominent ripples. The Braginskii case (C) yields intermediate suppression. We also vary the plasma $\beta$ parameter ($\beta \approx$ 100 and 1600) to examine how a changing magnetic field strength affects the results. Stronger magnetic fields further suppress KHI, leading to smoother fronts and reduced differences between different viscosity models, while also widening the range of permitted pressure anisotropies when microinstability-based limiters are present. These results indicate that both viscosity and magnetic fields play crucial roles in stabilising sloshing cold fronts in galaxy clusters.

papers.title: A targeted machine learning approach for detecting diffuse radio emission with Astronomaly: Protege
papers.summary: Diffuse radio emission in galaxy clusters, such as radio halos, relics, and mini halos, is a key tracer of non-thermal processes, turbulence, and magnetic fields within the intra-cluster medium. However, their low surface brightness, as well as contamination from compact sources and imaging artefacts, makes their detection challenging. The sheer volume of data from instruments such as the Square Kilometre Array will render traditional manual-inspection based detection methods infeasible. This paper introduces a novel machine learning approach that uses active learning to rapidly identify diffuse emission candidates from a small, optimally-selected subset of data. We apply the self-supervised deep learning algorithm Bootstrap Your Own Latent to extract features from source cutouts in the MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey (MGCLS). We then pass these features through the Astronomaly: Protege anomaly detection framework to identify the final candidates. Using a human-labelled set, we evaluate our pipeline on high-resolution (~ 7''), convolved (15''), and combined-feature MGCLS datasets. Interestingly, the high-resolution features identify diffuse sources more efficiently than the convolved resolution, which are in turn outperformed by the combined features. Of the top 100 sources ranked by Protege, 98% exhibit diffuse characteristics, with 53% confirmed as cluster-related emission. Our work shows that Protege can identify diffuse emission with minimal human labelling effort, offering a powerful, scalable tool capable of detecting both known and novel diffuse radio sources.

papers.title: oMEGACat. IX. Chemical Tagging of Omega Centauri Populations with Machine-Learning-Inferred Abundances from the MUSE Spectrograph
papers.summary: We present chemical abundance measurements for 7,302 red giant branch stars within the half-light radius (~5') of $\omega$ Centauri ($\omega$ Cen), derived from MUSE spectra using the neural network model DD-Payne. DD-Payne effectively identifies spectral features of C, N, and O for [Fe/H]>-1.0 dex; Mg for [Fe/H]>-1.5 dex; and Na, Ca, and Ba for all metallicities. By combining these measurements with previous high-resolution studies, we create the most comprehensive picture of $\omega$ Cen's rich chemical evolutionary history. For the first time, we map elemental variations across the entire chromosome diagram, which is widely used to identify multiple populations. We analyze the median chemical abundance trends as functions of age and metallicity for different subpopulations. The DD-Payne measurements of [C/Fe], [N/Fe], and [O/Fe] extend literature trends to higher metallicities and show continuous abundance-metallicity relations, with [(C+N+O)/Fe] increasing steadily with [Fe/H]. [Ca/Fe] and the s-process element [Ba/Fe] also increase with metallicity across all populations. For [Ba/Fe], the chemically enhanced (P2) populations are more enriched than primordial (P1) and the intermediate (Im) populations. Furthermore, [N/Fe] correlates strongly with stellar age while [Ca/Fe] and [Ba/Fe] exhibit a weaker age dependence. Using these abundance-metallicity-age relations, we evaluate formation scenarios of $\omega$ Cen proposed in the literature and find none fully explains all the observed relations. Our study demonstrates that combining MUSE with machine learning enables large-sample stellar abundance measurements in crowded cluster cores, overcoming the limitations of fiber-fed spectroscopy for studying multiple stellar populations and their evolutionary histories.

papers.title: Testing the isothermal Jeans model for self-interacting dark matter halos in the collapse phase
papers.summary: We benchmark the semi-analytical isothermal Jeans model against a high-resolution isolated N-body simulation that follows a self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halo into deep core collapse. The model accurately reproduces the density evolution through much of the collapse phase, although it does not capture the sharp rise in central velocity dispersion during collapse. When applied to strong gravitational lensing observables, such as the projected mass and logarithmic density slope of SIDM halos, the Jeans model tracks the simulated evolution more closely than the parametric approach in the deep collapse regime. Our results demonstrate that the isothermal Jeans model provides a reliable and computationally efficient description of SIDM halo evolution.

papers.title: Stars with Plumbing Issues: The Multi-component Ejecta of Common Envelopes
papers.summary: Common-envelope evolution (CEE) is one of the major open problems in binary stellar evolution, even though it is the primary channel for forming close binaries with at least one compact object. While CEE is often assumed to lack direct observational constraints, recent connections between CEE and the transient class, luminous red novae (LRNe), as well as the post-AGB systems known as Water Fountains (WFs), provide new opportunities to understand how this event unfolds. Collectively, these observations suggest that envelope ejection during CEE is neither spherically symmetric nor homologous, but rather produces complex ejecta, providing constraints for simulations of CEE. In this work, we present a series of three-dimensional hydrodynamical (non-MHD) simulations of CEE for a 2 Msun red-giant-branch (RGB) star and show that the event naturally produces multi-component ejecta including an extended radially expanding shell, a thick circumbinary disk (CBD), and collimated bipolar outflows. Consistent with previous works in the literature, the bipolar outflows in our simulations arise naturally through geometrical constraints imposed by the disk and do not require magnetic fields. While we find that the formation of the collimated outflows can be sensitive to the choice of Riemann solver, they appear across all resolutions and mass ratios tested in this work. We show that the multi-component ejecta formed during CEE simulations naturally reproduce some of the key properties of CEE observations, including the classical bipolar shape seen in some LRNe, WFs, and planetary nebulae.

papers.title: From photometric surveys to HI intensity mapping: Improving constraints on magnification biases while testing gravity
papers.summary: The observed large-scale structure of the Universe is not a direct measure of the underlying distribution of matter. These observations are subtly distorted by gravitational lensing effects, which leave imprints on the statistical distribution of galaxies and offer a powerful test of general relativity. In this work, we investigate whether HI intensity mapping from current and forthcoming surveys can improve constraints on magnification lensing obtained from photometric galaxy surveys. In particular, we investigate whether one can jointly constrain the magnification bias parameters $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ and the amplitude of the Weyl potential, which we parametrise as $\beta$. We employ a Fisher matrix formalism in order to estimate future constraints on the magnification biases and $\beta$. We forecast constraints for three photometric surveys (DES-like, LSST-like, Euclid-like) individually and together with two HI intensity mapping surveys (MeerKLASS, SKAO). We apply the multi-tracer technique by combining each galaxy survey with each HI survey, exploiting the combined constraining in the overlapping sky area. The multi-tracer approach dramatically improves constraints on $\beta$ by factors of 18 to 50, depending on the surveys considered. For $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$, improvements can be marginal or by factors of 2 to 4. We also verify that $\beta$ and $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ can be constrained simultaneously as the cross-correlations between tracers break the degeneracies among them. We conclude that the multi-tracer combination of photometric galaxy surveys and HI intensity mapping surveys enables high-precision measurements of both $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ and $\beta$. This opens an additional pathway to constrain $\Phi+\Psi$ and test the validity of general relativity on cosmological scales.

papers.title: Unveiling Hidden Lyman Alpha Emitters in the DESI DR1 Data
papers.summary: We present an automatic method based on machine-learning convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to detect Lyman alpha emitters (LAE) hidden in the Data Release 1 spectroscopic dataset of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Those LAEs mostly have incorrect redshift estimations because the current DESI pipeline is not designed to detect and measure the redshifts of galaxies at $z>2$. To uncover those sources, we first visually inspect thousands of DESI spectra and construct a sample, consisting of both LAEs and non-LAEs, for training and testing the CNN-based model to (1) detect LAEs in DESI spectra and (2) determine their Ly$\alpha$ redshifts. The final model yields $95.2\%$ purity and $95.9\%$ completeness for detecting LAEs. We apply this model to approximately $2\times10^{6}$ spectra of sources targeted as emission-line galaxies and detect 19,685 LAEs from $z\sim2$ to $3.5$ within 12 minutes with a single GPU, illustrating the high efficiency of this model for identifying LAEs. The detected LAEs are mostly at the bright end of the luminosity function with Ly$\alpha$ luminosity $L_{\rm Ly\alpha} \gtrsim 10^{43}$ erg/s. The high signal-to-noise composite spectrum of the detected LAEs further shows various spectral features, including P-Cygni profiles of metal lines and MgII emission lines, possible indicators of Lyman continuum escape fraction, revealing the rich astrophysical information in this LAE sample. Finally, this sample can be used to train and validate the pipelines for redshift determination of LAEs for the preparation of the DESI-II survey.

papers.title: The Metallicity Distribution of the Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxy Segue 1
papers.summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs; stellar masses $M_* < 10^5\,M_\odot$) offer unique insights into early chemical evolution in low-mass systems. However, interpreting their metallicity distribution functions (MDFs) has been challenging due to limited spectroscopic samples, especially beyond the red giant branch. We present metallicities from the CaII K absorption feature, measured from low-resolution ($R\sim1000$) Keck/LRIS spectroscopy of 40 stars in the UFD Segue 1 ($M_* \approx 500\,M_\odot$), including both red giant branch and main-sequence turnoff stars, resulting in a metallicity sample more than six times larger than previously published data for Segue 1. The resulting MDF has an average [Fe/H] $= -2.52 \pm 0.10$ dex and a dispersion of $\sigma = 0.59 \pm 0.06$ dex, and is best described by a single Gaussian, with no evidence for multimodal substructure. This is consistent with a continuous, short-duration ($\lesssim$1~Gyr) episode of star formation and chemical enrichment prior to reionization. The nonzero metallicity spread reaffirms its classification as a galaxy. Segue 1 highlights the rich chemical enrichment histories present even in the least massive galaxies, and underscores the importance of deep spectroscopic follow-up to fully characterize these ancient stellar systems.

papers.title: A 4200-hour HyperFlash and \'ECLAT campaign on the hyperactive FRB 20240114A: constraining energetics with the most brilliant bursts
papers.summary: Hyperactive repeaters provide a unique window into the evolving environments and energy budgets of fast radio burst (FRB) sources, though they may not be representative of the FRB population in general. High-cadence observations are key to capturing the rarest and most energetic bursts, which occur only once per hundreds to thousands of hours. Here we present an unprecedented $4{,}200$-hour observing campaign targeting FRB 20240114A as part of the HyperFlash and \'ECLAT FRB monitoring programs. Over $806$ days, we detected $178$ high-energy ($\sim$$10^{40-42}$ erg) bursts with HyperFlash, which together amount to $4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg of released radio energy (assuming isotropic emission and 1-GHz emission bandwidth). The cumulative energy of the HyperFlash bursts is about twice that of $\sim$$11{,}000$ lower-energy bursts detected with FAST, emphasising the significant role that the highest-energy bursts play in depleting the central engine's stored energy. In fact, the single most brilliant burst from our sample, which we term the STROOP, contributes roughly $1/3$ of all the energy we measure, and is at the maximum energy seen in studies of both repeating and apparently one-off FRBs alike. We also find a break in the burst energy distribution at $\sim$$2\times10^{40}$ erg and a linear dispersion measure (DM) increase of $+0.96 \pm 0.06$ pc cm$^{-3}$ over a period of $318$ days. We discuss these findings in the context of a magnetar source model and highlight comparisons with the energetics of intermediate and giant X-ray/$\gamma$-ray flares from Galactic sources.
