papers.title: Gradient-Based Optimization Enables Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Gate Synthesis
papers.summary: We develop a numerical approach to optimizing a quantum circuit over a discrete gate set by using gradient descent to tune $R_Z$ angles to a solution where many $R_Z$ gates can be rounded to a Clifford or $T$ gate without introducing further synthesis error. Our approach can adapt to any discrete gate set, which we demonstrate using the Clifford + $T$ + $\sqrt T$ gate set.

papers.title: Continuous-time evolution via probabilistic angle interpolation and its applications
papers.summary: We explore the applicability of a stochastic time-evolution algorithm based on probabilistic angle interpolation. To simplify the pre-processing of the algorithm, we take the continuous-time limit, thereby explicitly eliminating Trotter errors and streamlining the resource analysis. As demonstrations, we apply the algorithm to two representative problems: estimating the ground-state energy of the $H_3^+$ molecular Hamiltonian and computing out-of-time-ordered correlators in the sparse Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. We evaluate the protocol's performance through numerical simulations and experiments on a trapped-ion quantum computer, Quantinuum Reimei.

papers.title: Tight Quantum Lower Bound for k-Distinctness
papers.summary: In this paper, we introduce a new quantum query lower bound framework. It is inspired by Zhandry's compressed oracle technique, but it also subsumes the polynomial method as a special case. Compared to Zhandry's technique, our approach has two key differences. First, we do not use any oracles (except for the standard input oracle), and define ``knowledge'' directly through the expansion of the state of the algorithm in the Fourier basis. Second, we allow arbitrary probability distributions of inputs. We show how this framework behaves on the problem of finding equal elements in the input string. In particular, we demonstrate its power by proving a first tight quantum query lower bound for the k-Distinctness problem.

papers.title: A Logarithmic-Depth Quantum Multiplier
papers.summary: We present a quantum algorithm for multiplying two $n$-bit integers with overall circuit depth and $T$-depth both bounded by $O(\log n)$, while using $O(n^2)$ gates and ancillary qubits. Our construction generates partial products via indicator-controlled copying and adds them using a tree of reversible $3$-to-$2$ adders followed by one quantum carry-lookahead adder. Building on the carry-save adders of Kim et al., we combine full input fanout, workspace reuse, and phase-corrected gate implementations to reduce $T$-depth. We provide explicit circuit constructions, proofs of correctness, and concrete closed-form resource bounds.

papers.title: Entanglement Enhanced Sensing with Qubits affected by non-Markovian Dephasing
papers.summary: Entanglement has been proposed as a means to improve the sensitivity of sensing weak signals. While the degree of this quantum advantage is well understood in noiseless settings, the situation is more complex under realistic conditions, where the system is subject to decoherence. In this case, the enhancement depends on the specific noise characteristics. Previous treatments of colored noise typically assume that the noise is uncorrelated between successive experiments. Here, we consider the scenario in which the noise exhibits correlations across multiple shots. We derive a simple fundamental limit to the sensitivity based on the fact that the sensitivity cannot be better than the signal-to-noise ratio seen by the probe. Focusing on Ramsey spectroscopy with probes affected by pure classical dephasing, we show that, for suitable spatial and temporal noise correlations, entangled probes achieve a better scaling of the sensitivity with the number of probes than separable states. This demonstrates that entanglement can provide a substantial improvement for Ramsey spectroscopy subject to correlated noise.

papers.title: Quantum limit cycles with continuous symmetries from coherent parametric driving: exact solutions and many-body extensions
papers.summary: There is widespread interest in many-body quantum systems that exhibit limit-cycle or time-crystalline behaviour. An ideal quantum limit cycle would be realized using fully coherent driving (to minimize noise) and also have a continuous internal symmetry (to ensure generation of monochromatic radiation). While these two requirements may seem incompatible, we introduce in this work a large class of multi-mode bosonic limit cycle models based on coherent parametric driving which possess an O(N) continuous symmetry. Surprisingly, the full quantum dissipative steady state of these models can be found exactly. They exhibit rich physics, including steady state entanglement, reduced phase diffusion and the possibility of realizing quantum limit tori. The basic mechanism we identify provides a unified way to understand how coherent parametric driving can yield symmetry-enriched limit cycles, and also helps us understand related models where the relevant symmetries are weakly broken. The models we study are compatible with a range of different experimental platforms, including quantum optical setups and superconducting quantum circuits.

papers.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
papers.summary: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. We first give a self-contained derivation of the Fokker--Planck equation that governs the time evolution of the mixing measure for a Gaussian mixture. Then, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture to study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.

papers.title: A measure for genuine tripartite entanglement
papers.summary: We introduce a real-valued functional $I(\vec{n}_1,\vec{n}_2)$ of four three-qubit correlations that turns the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) algebraic paradox into a quantitative witness of genuine tripartite entanglement. For every three-qubit state $\rho$ and every pair of directions, $|I(\vec{n}_1,\vec{n}_2;\rho)|\le 2$, with equality if and only if $\vec{n}_1\perp\vec{n}_2$ and $\rho$ is locally unitarily equivalent to the GHZ state. On the five-parameter Ac\'in family, $I(\hat{x},\hat{y})$ depends only on $\lambda_0\lambda_4$ and is maximised by the GHZ state; for the W state $I(\hat{x},\hat{y})=0$ and $\max|I_{\mathrm{W}}|=35/27$. Maximising over independent local orthonormal frames yields a local-unitary invariant measure $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{GHZ}}\in[0,1]$, computable from four three-body Pauli correlators, that equals one exactly on the GHZ orbit and takes the values $35/54$ on the W state and $1/2$ on product states. We show that $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ is not convex: an equal mixture of three biseparable states has $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{GHZ}}=14/27$, larger than the average $1/2$ of its components. We also relate $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ to GHZ fidelity witnesses, discuss its behaviour under local operations and classical communication, and outline a generalisation to three qudits via Heisenberg-Weyl operators.

papers.title: Ensemble Engineering to Overcome Destructive Cancellation in Quantum Measurements
papers.summary: Quantum state preparation can shape how positive and negative contributions combine in correlation measurements, providing a route to control cancellation through ensemble engineering. We develop a framework for relating this control to the prepared distribution, using the infinite-temperature trace of the same operator product as a uniform-weight reference for ensemble-dependent correlators. For diagonal observables, resolving both projector sectors separates each sector's probability mass from its conditional sign alignment and determines their contributions to the full correlator. A worked example shows what a selected-sector description can miss, and a simple bound limits the error from omitting the complementary contribution. We use two complementary preparations: Grover-type amplitude amplification to redistribute probability toward a specified target, and oracle-free shallow circuits to shape the distribution at low depth. Zero-time benchmarks combine noiseless simulations with finite-shot sampling and IBM Quantum demonstrations on up to 20 qubits. Sector statistics distinguish low occupation from cancellation within an occupied sector, while comparisons with noiseless simulations show that characteristic features of the engineered cumulative patterns persist on hardware. We also extend the analysis to multi-qubit diagonal observables and connect their sign and sector rules to explicit preparation choices. These results provide a basis for designing and assessing structured ensembles through their operator-resolved contributions to quantum correlation measurements.

papers.title: Degree-Guided Adiabatic Quantum Algorithm for MIS with Neutral Atoms
papers.summary: We present a quantum adiabatic algorithm for solving MIS with Rydberg atoms, which uses graph degrees to engineer the Hamiltonian for adiabatic evolution. Our approach extends the algorithm of Pichler et al. for MIS state preparation, which uses time-dependent global controls to excite atoms while the Rydberg blockade mechanism suppresses adjacent excitations. To accelerate adiabatic evolution, we introduce local light shifts that favor excitation of low-degree nodes and constrain the final Hamiltonian so that energy scales inversely with the number of Rydberg excitations, preventing convergence to non-MIS states. Benchmarking our degree-dependent MIS algorithm with the traditional adiabatic algorithm on a set of 1000 MIS instances, we demonstrate numerically that our algorithm inflates the minimal spectral gap and, consequently, accelerates the convergence. By fitting power-law relations for both the time-to-solution and success probability metrics as a function of the hardness parameter, we demonstrate a superior scaling exponent for our algorithm over the traditional global protocol. Furthermore, the classical Hamiltonian engineering step required to construct degree-dependent controls introduces only polynomial overhead. These results indicate that our algorithm can be used to extend the size of graphs for which MIS can be found on physical hardware. Moreover, our approach extends beyond MIS to additional graph problems such as MAX-CUT.

papers.title: Quantum Quenches that Resemble Operator Growth
papers.summary:
We study growth quenches, which are local quenches that may gradually destabilize a false vacuum in certain kinetic constrained quantum lattice models, such as the East-West model. We point out a formal analogy with the dynamics of a local operator in the Heisenberg picture. Exploiting this analogy, we obtain several results on growth quenches by adapting operator-dynamics concepts and methods. First, applying the Krylov approach (recursion method), we conjecture the linear growth of Lanzcos coefficients in generic quenches, $a_m \sim 
u m$ (diagonal), and $b_m \sim \alpha m$ (off-diagonal), extending an operator growth hypothesis. We show that the growth quench dynamics is localized in both Krylov and Fock spaces when $|
u| > 2 \alpha$, and derive a bound for the growth quench analogue of Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L \le \sqrt{4 \alpha^2 - 
u^2}$ when $|
u| < 2 \alpha$. Second, we realize the Fock localization in large $N$ solvable growth quenches inspired by Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The bound on Lyapunov exponent is saturated in large-$q$ SYK grow quench. By contrast, the growth quench is almost always Fock localized in a nonrandom all-to-all growth quench amenable to semiclassics. Finally, in the 1D East-West model, we interpret Fock space cage states as the existence of a conserved charge. We show that the latter has ballistic transport due to current conservation. Moreover, adding hopping with a fine-tuned amplitude induces a partial localization due to a flat band. Our work suggest growth quenches as a promising approach to realize non-equilibrium coherent phenomena in many-body systems.

papers.title: Quantum geometry of connected state manifolds: When diabolic points act as bridges between eigenstate manifolds
papers.summary: Parametric Hamiltonians often exhibit point-like spectral degeneracies, called diabolic points (DPs) or conical intersections, which can lead to singularities in the Provost-Vallee metric of eigenstate manifolds. We regularise the metric by a transformation to polar coordinates and develop a formalism in which DPs act as bridges between adjacent eigenstate manifolds, glueing them into a single connected state manifold (CSM). We characterise the topology of this structure and extend the local rules for nodal lines governing the Berry phase to global ones. On the CSM, the class of geodesics can be enlarged by those passing through the DPs. They can be stable with respect to their initial direction, and can be shorter than those constrained to a single eigenstate manifold, providing new geodesic shortcuts. Further, the CSM provides a new mechanism for Berry phase computation along paths traversing the DPs.

papers.title: How To Track Qubits Through Space and Time (Or: Sailing in a Quantum Boat)
papers.summary: While quantum position verification aims to certify a prover's location using quantum information, existing security definitions only guarantee that part of the successful adversarial party is in the claimed location. This leaves open the possibility that a distributed team of adversaries can jointly simulate a prover in a way that defeats the intended meaning of `being at a location' in position-based cryptography. We introduce stronger notions of position verification that we call quantum localization, which requires that there is a specified, unclonable state at the verified spacetime point-and that this state can be found nowhere else. We show that quantum localization leads naturally to a meaningful notion of trajectory verification, in which quantum information is verifiably tracked through space and time. We construct quantum localization and trajectory verification protocols using quantum anchor states, which generalize coset states from unclonable cryptography. The security of our schemes is proven in the classical oracle (i.e. ideal obfuscation) model, which can be heuristically instantiated in the plain model using post-quantum indistinguishability obfuscation. We also introduce and instantiate the concept of functionality localization, which guarantees that the adversary has the ability to compute a secret function at the verified spacetime point, and this function cannot be computed anywhere else. This raises the intriguing possibility of localizing computational capabilities in space and time. More broadly, we believe our notions of quantum localization and subsequent feasibility results provide stronger foundations for position-based cryptography. At a conceptual level, our results also explore the tight link between two fundamental notions in physics-location and information-thus serving as a natural foundation for cryptographic capabilities tied to physical spacetime.

papers.title: A Compass on the Quantum State Sphere: The Hopf Ansatz for Arbitrary Pure-State Optimization
papers.summary: Optimizing an arbitrary pure state requires more than a circuit that can prepare it: one also needs coordinates, local distance information, and measurable derivative directions. We introduce the Hopf ansatz, a binary-tree circuit for arbitrary normalized real and complex state vectors. Internal angles split probability between subtrees, while leaf phases supply the complex degrees of freedom. The same tree recovers physical angles from known amplitudes, gives an analytic diagonal metric on the state-vector sphere, and prepares each nonzero coordinate tangent as a normalized state. For Hamiltonian objectives and other costs with the same local transition-moment form, each gradient component is a known metric factor times a transition moment between the current state and a tangent state. Signed branch states express these moments through expectation-value measurements. Indexed preparation groups magnitude tangents by tree depth and collects complex phase tangents into one leaf-indexed block. The number of compiled gradient-access circuit families is logarithmic in Hilbert-space dimension; measurement repetitions needed for a prescribed accuracy remain a separate statistical cost. In deterministic real-state benchmarks with exact objectives and gradients and known global optima, metric-aware Hopf updates reach numerical-precision median gaps. Relative to coordinate-Adam baselines, they yield smaller mean final gaps in variational eigensolver tests and concentrate more runs at numerical precision in metrology-inspired tests. The Hopf ansatz thus supplies a compass for arbitrary pure-state optimization, with coordinates, geometry, and measurable directions in one circuit structure.

papers.title: Geometric power capacity of coherent ergotropy in quantum batteries
papers.summary: We explore coherent ergotropy extraction in quantum batteries from a resource-geometric point of view. For an initial state $\rho$, we quantify the coherent extraction process by the coherent ergotropy $\mathcal{E}_c(\rho)$ and the coherent extraction distance $D_c^{\rm ext}(\rho)$ between the active state $\sigma_\rho$ and the passive state $P_\rho$. This defines the geometric power capacity $\Pi_c(\rho)=\mathcal{E}_c(\rho)/D_c^{\rm ext}(\rho)$, which measures the coherent ergotropy released unit minimal unitary distance. We prove that, for any driving Hamiltonian satisfying $\|V_t\|\leq\nu$, the actual coherent discharging power is bounded by $P_c^{\rm ext}(\rho;V_t)\leq \nu\Pi_c(\rho)$, showing that $\Pi_c(\rho)$ is a capacity under unit driving norm rather than the power of a particular protocol. General bounds on $\Pi_c(\rho)$ are derived by combining relative entropy bounds on coherent ergotropy with geometric bounds on the coherent extraction distance. We also formulate coherence measure induced bounds and protocol-corrected capacities involving the effective speed of a given Hamiltonian. Qubit and qutrit examples demonstrate that $\Pi_c(\rho)$ captures a resource-geometric feature of coherent discharging beyond coherent ergotropy or coherence measures alone.

papers.title: QSCI-CMP: Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction with Chemically Motivated Preselection
papers.summary: We present QSCI-CMP, a quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for molecular ground-state calculations that reduces both the query count and the gate count of sample-based quantum diagonalization with amplitude amplification (SQD-AA). SQD-AA mitigates the measurement bottleneck of quantum-selected configuration interaction (QSCI) by amplifying the basis states that have not yet been measured. Its oracle, however, specifies the measured states by listing them one by one, so its gate count grows with the number of collected states. Moreover, the quantum resources are spent even on states whose importance is evident from chemical knowledge, such as low-order excitations from the Hartree-Fock reference, which could be collected classically at the outset. We therefore propose to fix such chemically trivial states in advance, include them in the diagonalization subspace from the start, and exclude them from the amplification target, using a low-cost oracle that recognizes them through the excitation level and the seniority number of each basis state. We numerically demonstrate that QSCI-CMP reduces the query count and the gate count required to reach chemical accuracy by up to approximately 68% and 72% relative to SQD-AA for 24-qubit systems. The chemically trivial subspace is freely tunable within the classical computational budget. A larger subspace shifts more work onto the classical solver and increases the reduction in quantum cost, and when it captures the ground state sufficiently well, no quantum sampling is needed at all. We also point out that a query-optimal iteration count known from the analysis of quantum search further reduces the query count of both methods by approximately 12%.

papers.title: The exact price of local realism in CHSH experiments: a measurement-dependence-detection trade-off surface, a moir\'e phase-locking mechanism that saturates it, and an unmeasured fringe in the fourfold coincidence sum
papers.summary: For local hidden-variable accounts of the CHSH experiment that are faithful -- reproducing the observed singles and coincidence rates and unbiased marginals of a polarization singlet with symmetric detector efficiency $\eta_{\rm eff}$ -- I determine the minimal measurement dependence $M$ (Hall's measure) needed to reach a CHSH value $S$. Linear programming over all local strategies yields, to machine precision, $M(S,\eta_{\rm eff})=\max\{0,\eta_{\rm eff}((S+2)\eta_{\rm eff}-4)/6\}$, whose edges reproduce Hall's bound, the Garg-Mermin threshold, and the postselection ceiling. The quantum point is certified exactly: $M(2\sqrt{2},9/10)=(27\sqrt{2}-33)/100$, by primal and dual certificates in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$. I solve the unique detection profile under which a deterministic sign model reproduces the singlet exactly, and prove exact quantum correlations and angle-independent coincidence rates jointly impossible in this class. Mixtures of this profile with measurement dependence trade $M$ against a $\cos 4(a-b)$ modulation of the fourfold coincidence sum, up to 12.4% in relative amplitude, taking identical values at the two CHSH relative angles; existing data exclude its full amplitude and bound its mixtures with flat detection to a detection share of order 15%; its sub-percent content is unbounded. A two-setting cross-ratio and a settings-torus log-Fourier protocol, both calibrated against channel-efficiency imbalance, reach $5\sigma$ at 0.1% within hours: a flat result excludes the solved family to a detection share of order 1%; a surviving fringe would be a joint $(a,b)$ dependence no single-pair apparatus produces. I exhibit a local mechanism, moir\'e phase locking, with deterministic phase evolution and randomness in a quenched ensemble, which attains the certified floor exactly at $\eta_{\rm eff}=1$ and, with the solved profile, reaches $M=0$ at $\eta_{\rm eff}\approx 0.80$.

papers.title: Quantifying Nonstabilizerness of Codeword-Stabilized Codes
papers.summary: Universal quantum computation requires non-Clifford gates, which stabilizer codes can provide transversally only up to a finite level of the Clifford hierarchy. Non-stabilizer codes are not subject to this bound and are the natural candidates to fill the gap. However, it is difficult to efficiently evaluate the nonstabilizerness (or magic) of non-stabilizer codes. Here, we resolve this problem for codeword-stabilized (CWS) codes by showing that the nonstabilizerness of a CWS code is determined by the difference structure of its codewords. Whenever a Sidon set of the required size exists, the most magical codes are related to the Sidon sets, whose pairwise differences are all distinct. Structural analysis demonstrates that nonstabilizerness is invariant under coset closure, giving rise to non-stabilizer codes with arbitrarily many logical qubits and constant nonstabilizerness. Nonstabilizerness of whole code families becomes exactly computable, and we obtain closed-form values for the Kerdock codes. Moreover, we reveal a tradeoff between nonstabilizerness and transversal gates. For a code with $k$ logical qubits, a diagonal transversal gate that is non-Clifford on $t$ coordinates forces the nonstabilizerness benchmark to be at most $2(k-t)$. These results reduce the search for codes with high nonstabilizerness and for transversal non-Clifford gates to classical counting problems, to which the standard tools of additive combinatorics apply.

papers.title: Exact quantum splitting and the structure of finite algebras
papers.summary: For squarefree $f\in\F_q[x]$, Berlekamp's fixed-point algebra is $B\cong\F_q^r$, where $r$ is the number of irreducible factors. We give an exact quantum splitting procedure in a circuit model permitting efficiently computable, input-dependent single-qubit rotations. For a block with $s\ge2$ factors, a quadratic-character test (odd $q$) or absolute-trace test (characteristic $2$) is nonconstant with an exactly known probability $p_{q,s}\ge1/2$. Its value depends only on $q,s$, not on the hidden factors. An auxiliary-qubit reduction to success probability $1/4$ makes one Grover iteration exact. Thus factorization takes exactly $r-1$ splitting rounds and $O(n^3\log q)$ quantum $\F_q$-operations, with deterministic polynomial classical preprocessing and bookkeeping. The method also extracts primitive idempotents of arbitrary finite-dimensional commutative unital algebras given by structure constants in $O(n^4\log q)$ quantum $\F_q$-operations, staying over $\F_q$ throughout. Computing the radical and passing to the center extends it to the decomposition of $A/\Rad(A)$ into simple two-sided ideals, for an arbitrary finite-dimensional associative $\F_q$-algebra $A$.

papers.title: Predictive Structure Behind Rare Outcomes in Random Quantum Circuits
papers.summary: Local random quantum circuits selected for unusually large output peaks reveal intermediate-state structure that predicts new peak formation and guides circuit construction. In one-dimensional Haar-random brickwall circuits, the selected trajectories combine stronger pairwise correlations and probability redistribution with lower bipartite entanglement and output entropy. We test the predictive value of this structure by keeping each circuit's initial segment fixed and independently regenerating the remaining gates. Across the tested size-depth grid at n=8-14, peak-selected states have higher new-peak probability than normal/nonpeak controls, with an overall probability ratio of 3.23 at the primary depths. Within a separate unconditioned ensemble, a fixed structural score computed from the initial segment predicts new-peak probability and gives a 1.86-fold yield gain in a replay with equal numbers of remaining-circuit evaluations. Randomizing relative phases while preserving computational-basis probabilities strongly attenuates the selected-state advantage, demonstrating a functional contribution from relative-phase organization. Structural and phase-intervention tests extend to n=16. Structure-guided gate selection improves high-peak yield under common local refinement, while guidance using multiple intermediate observables improves new-peak probability over peak-only guidance in all 16 tested size-depth settings. Together, these results show how intermediate-state structure can predict and promote new peak formation under finite-depth local dynamics.

papers.title: clifford_qc: A Python Toolkit for Quantum Simulation
papers.summary: clifford_qc is a Python research toolkit for constructing quantum models, comparing variational and subspace eigensolvers, and estimating measurement resources. A common sparse Pauli algebra connects Hamiltonians, density operators, gates, and candidate-selection observables; dedicated interfaces handle circuits, execution, and statistical estimates. A worked gradient example illustrates shared measurements, and a molecular workflow separates reusable preparation, solving, and reference validation. Matrix-element banks support virtual subspaces, exact Ritz residuals, and folded-spectrum roots. Process-isolated benchmarks show that packed coefficients and streaming reduce observed peak memory on the larger tested inputs at increased runtime. Measurement studies separate setting counts, shot requirements, and device cost: fully commuting readout certifies a fixed first-order Ritz functional with fewer shots, while anticommuting cliques help some fixed reference energies and not others. Entangling-gate time and connectivity can offset shot savings or make a protocol inadmissible under illustrative device models. Further studies expose subspace bias, indeterminate encoding comparisons, failed approximate-restriction screens, and high residual-measurement costs under the tested uniform allocations. Generated tables, provenance records, a versioned evidence contract, and manuscript checks connect claims to their inputs. These small-system results support reproducible method development and establish neither hardware performance nor a general simulation speedup.

papers.title: A sharp norm inequality for entanglement-breaking channels
papers.summary: For a channel $\Phi$ on $M_d$ written in the generalised Bloch parameterisation $r \mapsto Ar+c$, we prove that entanglement breaking implies $\|A\|_*^2 + \frac{d(d-1)}{2}\,|c|^2 \;\le\; (d-1)^2 ,$ where $\|\cdot\|_*$ denotes the nuclear norm. Read on the Choi state of the channel, the inequality is an instance of the covariance-matrix criterion of Gittsovich et al.; what is added here is an elementary proof in Holevo form and a complete description of the equality cases. Apart from the constant channel onto a pure state, which shows that the coefficient $d(d-1)/2$ cannot be increased, equality holds exactly for the measure-and-prepare channels with rank-one effects $\alpha_k|e_k\rangle\langle e_k|$ and pure outputs $|\psi_k\rangle\langle\psi_k|$ whose overlaps are an affine image of those of the measurement directions, $|\langle\psi_j|\psi_k\rangle|^2 = P + (1-P)\,(d|\langle e_j|e_k\rangle|^2 - 1)/(d-1)$ for a common $P = \mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi(\mathbf{1}/d)^2$. These include the completely dephasing channel, the re-preparation channel of every rank-one POVM, a one-parameter family interpolating between dephasing and the constant channel, and non-unital non-projective examples already at $d = 2$. The qubit case reads $\|A\|_*^2+|c|^2\le1$ and extends to full rank a rank-two condition of Ruskai. The proof sharpens Ruskai's bound $\|A\|_*\le1$ by retaining the POVM completeness relation $\sum_k f_k=0$, which her argument discards; this recentres $A$ from a second moment into a cross-covariance, and is the entire content of the improvement.

papers.title: Universal holonomic control of algebras of observables
papers.summary: We extend geometric parallel transport from states and degenerate eigenspaces to observable algebras defining generalized quantum subsystems. At fixed block structure, unitary invariance fixes a unique connection, recovering Berry--Wilczek--Zee transport on bands. On positive-dimensional strata, its holonomy is the special-unitary part of the normalizer: all inner logical gates and equal-type sector permutations are attainable. Given a compatible gapped Hamiltonian and access to the required paths, inner gates can be implemented adiabatically by isospectral control of a band refinement.

papers.title: Qaiji IR: An Eight-Layer Intermediate Representation Family for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Compilation
papers.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical compilation relates ideal operations and measurement outcomes to control pulses and device instructions. Existing formats each describe part of this process, and their preservation checks are often specific to one tool rather than to a common intermediate representation (IR). I present Qaiji-IR, an eight-layer IR family organized by a five-axis semantic contract for data, semantics, lowering, runtime, and verification. Its implementation provides typed circuits, an operation-semantics layer (L4) that records operation structure and checks a bounded set of equivalence rules, and a native-scheduling layer (L2) with separate validation. Nine circuit pairs are compared with ideal reference calculations. An aggregate baseline, which compares operation categories and measurement counts, accepts four behavior-changing transformations: gate reordering and changes of rotation angle, operand, or measurement destination. The L4 checker passes none of them. It distinguishes strict equality from equality up to global phase and returns unsupported when its rules cannot decide, as for valid rotation fusion. L2 validation checks native schedules against their source circuits, decomposition rules, local matrices, and configured timing. A single-qubit active-reset program is compiled through the Qaiji-IR frontend, a syntax adapter, and the EmuPlat backend into pulses and device instructions for a virtual pulse processing unit (VPPU). Injected binary outcomes select the conditional drive. Backend predicate tests reveal incorrect execution for equality to zero and for a nonbinary feedback value. This backend path does not use the validated L2 schedule. Physical measurement feedback, calibrated pulse fidelity, and feedback latency require further work.

papers.title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
papers.summary: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to establish code families with constant encoding rate and linear distance, simultaneously achieving optimal asymptotic scaling in both parameters. In particular, we characterize explicit logical representatives of the full gauged code space, and provide a fundamental treatment of non-Abelian code distance in the sense of Knill--Laflamme based on combining expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary errors. We further construct an almost-good family with entire code spaces exhibiting long-range magic. Moreover, we use linearly addressable cup product to directly generate linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements of Clifford operators. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting, lay the foundation for pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture and shed light on non-Abelian quantum phases and orders beyond geometric locality.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for the exponentiation of Toeplitz matrices and applications in partial differential equations
papers.summary: We present quantum algorithms to approximate the exponential of banded Toeplitz matrices. These matrices have central importance in many PDE related problems, but their quantum implementation is hindered by their possibly large norms. Constructing directly the exponential we can circumvent this limitation. By relating the lower/upper shift operators to circulant and skewcirculant generators, which are diagonalised by the QFT, we construct (i) an LCU-based block encoding of banded Toeplitz matrices, (ii) an efficient, controllably truncated Pauli-string decomposition of the circulant eigenphases with a closed-form error bound, and (iii) a specialized QFT-Trotter product formula. As an application we build a block encoding of the propagator of the discretised heat equation with periodic, Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, using a frequency cutoff.

papers.title: Quantum--classical break-even in electronic dynamics of macrocyclic molecules
papers.summary: Here we demonstrate quantum--classical break-even for chemical dynamics applications, reaching useful accuracy with a quantum-hardware wall-clock time comparable to that estimated for practical classical computing resources. To this end, we develop a workflow for problems that are hardware-native but classically hard. We target large ring-shaped molecules that map naturally onto quantum hardware with neighboring connections. Exploiting the spatial locality of interactions, we compress short-time evolution within a small region using tensor networks. We then use rotational symmetry to replicate the compressed circuit in space and time, enabling long-time dynamics of large systems with practical classical processing times. We apply the workflow to conjugated macrocycles with rotational periodicity, 12-qubit benzene and 120-qubit [60]annulene, by embedding their electronic structure onto loops of IBM quantum processors. For the annulene, we compared the quantum-processing-unit (QPU) wall-clock times for hole-doped nonequilibrium dynamics to the estimated wall-clock time of two state-of-the-art classical methods, Majorana propagation and matrix-product-state time evolution based on the time-dependent variational principle. We show a situation in which a hybrid quantum--classical strategy is comparable to a classical-only counterpart in terms of both accuracy and computational time for a conventional high-performance computing system under ideal parallelization. These results show that quantum hardware can become a realistic computational option for chemical simulations for practitioners in chemical science and engineering.

papers.title: Real-Time Adaptive Filtering and the Boxcar Limit in Superconducting Qubit Readout
papers.summary: Control and readout systems for superconducting quantum computing support real-time control and high-fidelity qubit-state discrimination. We examine when additional digital processing improves readout fidelity. A common baseline for dispersive readout uses a boxcar averager to compute a uniformly weighted average over a fixed window followed by threshold-based state assignment. We evaluated an adaptive finite-impulse-response (FIR) filter trained in real time using the least-mean-squares (LMS) algorithm on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) quantum controller. We also analyzed measured readout shots offline to compare the frozen filter with boxcar averaging, and evaluate per-sample weighting plus sequential detection. For the fixed FIR filters tested, summing the filtered samples gives the boxcar sum multiplied by one complex number apart from a small edge correction. We call this the kernel collapse. The multiplication scales the state separation and noise equally without improving state discrimination, and we call this the boxcar limit. The frozen LMS filter reduces trace noise, but shows no resolved improvement in readout fidelity. On a 2D transmon, optimizing the readout window accounted for much of the improvement over full-window integration. We then examined how changing the decision method could reduce calibration effort and decision time. On a higher-fidelity 3D ancilla readout, our modeled template estimation reached the same fidelity target as direct averaging with 89.8% fewer labeled shots per state. Offline sequential replay assigned most shots before the acquisition window ended. These results distinguish waveform denoising from state-discrimination improvement, and motivate direct control of decision weights and assignment time in dispersive readout.

papers.title: Nonlinear quantum multi-spin dynamics without entanglement
papers.summary: We introduce a distinct route for extending classical atomistic spin dynamics into the quantum regime for arbitrary spin $s$, based on a variational product-state \textit{ansatz} that includes both pure and mixed local states. By construction, intersite entanglement -- expected to remain negligible even on very short time scales in many real materials -- is excluded, while local quantum effects are retained through the nonclassical structure of $s\geq 1$ density operators. Nonlinear dynamics arise from both the mean-field interdependence of the local states and the state-dependent dissipative terms. The framework recovers classical spin dynamics for $s=\frac{1}{2}$ while allowing genuinely quantum local dynamics for higher spins. It clarifies the variational and geometric origin of the inequivalence between quantum Landau-Lifshitz and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, provides a criterion for their equivalence under a common time rescaling, establishes connections with the classical theory through two qualitatively distinct limits ($s\to\infty$ and a large number of quantum spins $N$), and allows realistic $\mathcal{O}(N)$ simulations of quantum spin dynamics in materials.

papers.title: Characterizing Fermionic Non-Gaussianity in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model via Replica Twist Entropy
papers.summary: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems plays a central role in modern many-body physics. Intriguing insights emerge from investigating how quantum resources, which are essential for achieving unambiguous quantumness, are generated and spread under chaotic quantum dynamics. In fermionic systems, non-Gaussianity constitutes an important resource beyond entanglement, characterizing the deviation of generic quantum states from free-fermion states. In this Letter, we propose using the \textit{replica twist entropy}, defined through the expectation value of a replica rotation operator with a tunable angle $\alpha$, as a natural probe of non-Gaussianity in pure fermionic states. After deriving its behavior for typical many-body states, we establish a general framework for analyzing the replica twist entropy in solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models in the large-$N$ limit. Applying this framework to the dynamics of the thermofield double state, we uncover a novel dynamical phase diagram in the parameter space of $\alpha$ and evolution time $t$, exhibiting spontaneous $Z_2$ symmetry breaking at $\alpha=\pi/4$ and universal cusps as a function of $\alpha$ in the long-time regime. Our results pave the way for studying non-Gaussianity in strongly correlated fermionic systems and reveal a new class of dynamical transitions probed by non-Gaussianity.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.summary: This is the second of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on Shelah's independence property. An observable without it has idealized responses of the first Baire class, and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy for Rosenthal compacta divides such observables into three classes, each containing a physical order. In the transverse-field Ising model, the spontaneous magnetization decides whether the family of magnetizations is stable or lies in the second class.

papers.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
papers.summary: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.

papers.title: Scalable Tomography of Coherent Noise via Stabilizer-Code Polarization
papers.summary: Coherent errors accumulate linearly rather than diffusively, making them invisible to Pauli-twirl-based char- acterization. It poses a central challenge for quantum error correction, yet its characterization typically requires multi-qubit process tomography whose cost grows exponentially with system size. We show that measurement- free error correction projects arbitrary few-qubit coherent noise onto a fixed single-logical-qubit effective chan- nel, enabling tomography at constant cost. Exploiting the polarization effects of bit-flip and phase-flip codes, we construct a concatenated effective-channel fingerprint and prove, by a parity-based contradiction argument, that the observation map is globally injective over a prescribed coherent-noise family; hence the underlying noise parameters are uniquely recovered without any sparsity or low-rank assumptions. The recovered coherent noise model can be fed into decoding algorithms; relative to independent noise priors, we expect this to reduce the logical error rate for surface-code decoders. The protocol offers a scalable route to coherent-noise identification whenever the noise admits a moderate-dimensional parameterization.

papers.title: Hankel Submatrices with Bounded Word Length: Dimension Tradeoffs in Probabilistic and Quantum Automata
papers.summary: We characterize the largest admissible side length of fixed-margin square Hankel submatrices generated by probabilistic realizations on a \(d\)-point carrier and quantum linear realizations on a \(d\)-dimensional Hilbert space, when prefix and suffix word lengths are bounded by \(T\). Using a four-symbol transition alphabet shared by all selected rows and columns, we show that, for fixed margins \(\lambda_2>0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2<1\), the corresponding side lengths satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) quantum realizations and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for probabilistic automata. Four unitary and four permutation transition maps attain the corresponding orders. At zero false-acceptance tolerance (\(\lambda_2=0\) with \(0\leq\lambda_1<1\)), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=\Theta(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). The upper bounds follow from state-space packing and word counting, while the lower bounds combine explicit transition tuples with Grassmannian and positive-rate codebooks whose existence follows from the probabilistic method. These results establish sharp dimension--word-length tradeoffs for bounded-word Hankel tables.

papers.title: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
papers.summary: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.

papers.title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
papers.summary: Bayesian inference enables self-consistent plasma parameter inversion in tokamak integrated data analysis by fusing multi-source diagnostics. However, under nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods, finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate typically relies on sampling methods whose high computational overhead precludes real-time plasma control. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Bayesian inversion framework using a Coherent Ising Machine (CIM)-a quantum computing architecture based on coupled degenerate optical parametric oscillators (DOPOs). With native all-to-all connectivity, the CIM directly maps the negative log-posterior potential onto a spin Hamiltonian and leverages quantum vacuum fluctuations for rapid state-space search during pitchfork bifurcation. Validated on plasma current profile inversion for the EAST tokamak, this method achieves a single-run solution time of approximately 1 ms. Although current qubit limits necessitate a block-wise iterative scheme that prevents full real-time execution today, rapidly scaling quantum hardware offers a clear pathway toward real-time tokamak control.

papers.title: On the geometry of quantum constrained systems
papers.summary: Geometric methods have proved useful in the Hamiltonian description of classical constrained systems. We develop the corresponding geometry for quantum constrained systems, using the formulation of quantum mechanics in which the space of rays $\Ps$ is a K\"ahler manifold and unitary transformations are its canonical transformations. The Dirac conditions $\hat C_i\Psi=0$ define the zero set of a single function $\Cq=\ev{\Mop}$, the expectation value of the master constraint operator. Our central identity is $\Cq=|\mu|^2+\tfrac12\|X_\mu\|^2$, where $\mu=(\ev{\hat C_i})$ is the moment map of the gauge action on $\Ps$ and $X_\mu$ its fundamental vector fields: the quantum condition imposes the classical-type condition $\mu=0$ \emph{and} the collapse of the gauge orbits to points. This explains why no second reduction is needed. The physical state space is a totally geodesic K\"ahler submanifold. $\Cq$ is a Morse--Bott function which gradient flow is heat-kernel-smeared group averaging, converges to the nearest-point projection onto physical states, and its fibres are invariant under the complexified gauge group. Physical observables are characterised to all orders by the double-commutator condition, which is equivalent to $[\hat O,\hat P_0]=0$, with $\hat P_0$ the projector onto physical states. When zero lies in the continuous spectrum, the gradient flow converges to Dirac states in the sense of Grundling and Hurst, and its large-time asymptotics reproduce the rigging map of refined algebraic quantization. Finally, pulled back along coherent states, $\Cq$ equals the classical master constraint plus an $O(\hbar)$ term given by the squared speed of the classical gauge orbits. Together these results connect the Dirac procedure, the master constraint programme, refined algebraic quantization and symplectic reduction within one geometric picture.

papers.title: Absorbing state transitions with long-range annihilation
papers.summary: We introduce a family of classical stochastic processes describing diffusive particles undergoing branching and long-range annihilation in the presence of a parity constraint. The probability for a pair-annihilation event decays as a power-law in the distance between particles, with a tunable exponent. Such long-range processes arise naturally in various classical settings, and increasingly play a role in the study of quantum dynamics: for example, quantum state preparation or error correction processes aim to prepare ordered ground states, which requires removing point-like excitations in pairs via non-local feedback operations conditioned on a global set of measurement outcomes. We analytically and numerically describe features of absorbing phases and phase transitions in this family of classical models as pairwise annihilation is performed at larger and larger distances. Notably, we find that the two canonical absorbing-state universality classes -- directed-percolation and parity-conserving -- are endpoints of a new line of universality classes with continuously varying critical exponents. These new classes follow from an interplay of long-range interactions and symmetries: decreasing the long-range exponent effectively weakens the local effects of global symmetry constraints. This competition significantly broadens known non-equilibrium phases and phase transitions.

papers.title: Nonlinear Landau levels in the almost-bosonic anyon gas
papers.summary: We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an average-field description becomes appropriate for the low-energy collective state of the gas. Namely, by means of a Hartree-Jastrow ansatz, we derive a two-parameter Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger energy functional which extends the well-known Gross-Pitaevskii / nonlinear Schr\"odinger density functional theory to the magnetic (anyonic) self-interaction. One parameter determines the total number of self-generated magnetic flux units in the system, and the other the effective strength of spin-orbit self-interaction. This latter interaction can be either attractive/focusing or repulsive/defocusing, and depends both on the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction and the relative length scale of the flux profile of the anyons. Densities and energies of ground and excited states are studied analytically and numerically for a wide range of the parameters and align well with a sequence of exact nonlinear Landau levels describing Jackiw-Pi self-dual solitons. With increasing flux, counter-rotating vortices are formed, enhancing the stability of the gas against collapse. Apart from clarifying the relations between various different anyon models that have appeared in the literature, our analysis sheds new light on the many-anyon spectral problem, and also exemplifies a novel supersymmetry-breaking phenomenon.

papers.title: Time-Dependent Wave-Packet Approach to Reactions for Quantum Computation
papers.summary: We describe a method for obtaining the scattering matrix for nuclear or chemical reactions on a finite lattice. Aside from the preparation of the initial and final states as wave packets, the only other operation required is unitary time evolution, making this approach ideal for simulations on quantum hardware. The central quantity is a time-dependent overlap between incoming and outgoing wave packets whose Fourier transform corresponds to the scattering matrix at fixed energy, from which one can calculate elastic and inelastic cross sections for reactions involving two interacting clusters. Working in Cartesian coordinates enables an efficient encoding of the problem on quantum hardware via the first quantization mapping, with favorable qubit scaling for describing asymptotic scattering states. Within this framework, we describe a quantum algorithm for probing the scattering amplitude through different angles, including the forward direction, which provides access to the total cross section via the optical theorem. We demonstrate our methods through a series of numerical examples, for both elastic and inelastic processes, comparing against exact calculations. The techniques we describe can more readily be extended to a large number of constituent particles than other existing approaches, once fault-tolerant quantum hardware becomes available.

papers.title: Boundary R\'enyi oscillations in the open XX chain
papers.summary: For the ground state of the semi-infinite XX chain with Fermi momentum $k_F$, we derive the extracted $2k_F$ contribution to the R\'enyi entropy of its first $\ell$ sites at fixed $\alpha>1$. Its phase $\sin[(2\ell+1)k_F]$ matches the Friedel oscillation at the entangling bond and becomes the even--odd alternation at half filling. An exact Hankel determinant reduction and Riemann--Hilbert analysis give every term $\mathcal{L}^{-(2q-1)/\alpha}$ for positive integers $q$ with $2q-1<\alpha$, where $\mathcal{L}=4\ell\sin k_F$, with an $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1})$ error within this extracted component for $k_F$ away from $0$ and $\pi$. At integer $\alpha=p\ge2$, exact factorization gives a finite sum over all roots with error $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1-1/p})$. We also determine the $2k_F$ terms of $\log Z_\alpha(\phi)$, where $Z_\alpha(\phi)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A^\alpha e^{i\phi Q_A})$, $\rho_A$ is the block's reduced density matrix, and $Q_A$ is its fermion number. At fixed nonzero flux $|\phi|<\pi$ with $2q-1\mp\phi/\pi\ne\alpha$, the two exponential terms have different decay powers. Exact factorization sharpens the integer result. These pointwise estimates do not justify projection to fixed charge. The uncharged sequence and the two leading charged terms agree with earlier generalized Fisher--Hartwig predictions. Numerical calculations at $p=4$ test the predicted subleading coefficients without an adjustable normalization.

papers.title: Quantum matter is weakly entangled at low energies
papers.summary: We construct upper bounds on entanglement entropies of many-body quantum states that have fixed energy expectation values with respect to local Hamiltonians. Our focus is on entanglement entropies of subsystems that make up approximately half of the full system. The upper bound on the von Neumann entanglement entropy is half the sum of the thermal entropies of two fictitious systems at the same temperature as one another, with an additional area-law contribution in some systems. The effective temperature is chosen such that the sum of the thermal energies of the two fictitious systems matches the constraint on the energy of the state in the original problem; at subextensive energies, this temperature decreases with increasing system size. Our upper bounds on R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies take an analogous form. These inequalities show that, in systems that are frustration-free (FF) and whose zero-temperature subsystem thermal entropies scale with surface areas (rather than subsystem volumes), ground states are area-law entangled. For physical models of quantum matter, which have well-defined specific heat capacities (and are not necessarily FF), our bounds provide a way to convert this thermodynamic data into constraints on pure-state entanglement at both subextensive and extensive energies. We also show that our general upper bounds on half-system entanglement entropies are optimal, up to subleading corrections, in systems with reflection symmetry and above a subextensive energy threshold. A key application of our results is to constrain the entanglement of quantum states relevant to simulations of zero-temperature response functions, which have energies of order unity. We prove that, in wide varieties of FF systems in two dimensions and higher, the contributions of excitations to von Neumann entanglement entropy are subleading compared with the contribution from the ground state.

papers.title: Real-space spectral functions of three-dimensional billion-size topological non-Hermitian matter with tensor networks
papers.summary: Non-Hermitian systems host unconventional topological phenomena, while real-space spectral calculations in three dimensions remain computationally challenging. Here, we develop a tensor-network framework that combines a quantics-based matrix-product-operator representation of large real-space tight-binding Hamiltonians with a non-Hermitian kernel polynomial method. The Hermitized spectral problem is retained within the compact tensor-network representation, enabling real-space spectral function calculations for systems exceeding one billion lattice sites. Using this approach, we investigate a three-dimensional non-Hermitian higher-order topological insulator and resolve its corner-mode spectral response on a billion-site lattice, demonstrating the scalability and computational reach of the method. By tuning the gain--loss strength, we identify distinct in-gap corner-mode features in the weak- and strong-gain--loss regimes. Our results establish a scalable tensor-network framework for real-space spectral calculations in exceptionally large non-Hermitian lattice systems.

papers.title: HybridQC: Hardware-Grounded Simulation of Tightly Integrated Hybrid Quantum-Classical Systems
papers.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical performance depends on how quantum processors share classical compute, controllers, memory, and communication links. Circuit simulators and provider measurements expose kernel and job behavior, but leave topology-level questions about controller bottlenecks, quantum capacity, and mixed-workload contention unanswered. We present HybridQC, a discrete-event simulator for configurable hybrid compute units (HCUs). Users specify resource graphs containing classical compute, memory, controllers, quantum annealing (QA) and digital quantum computing (DQC) devices, and links. Jobs become dependent stages for preparation, quantum execution, transfers, reconstruction, and postprocessing. Finite capacities and selectable scheduling policies determine where stages wait and overlap. Service profiles use measurements from D-Wave Advantage 1 and Advantage 2 and IBM Kingston, Marrakesh, and Fez, separating physical quantum-processor occupancy from cloud wall time. Mean absolute percentage errors are 3.92%-8.04% for D-Wave access time and 5.26%-19.01% for IBM quantum seconds. Balanced 10x HCU scaling improves makespan by 2.19x-3.42x, while policy choice changes makespan by 1.80x for a mixed workload with 20 jobs per workload family. Scaling depends on which inputs grow: 100x data growth yields median runtime near 306 s, while 100x joint growth in circuits, shots, and depth reaches 4.806 x 10^7 s on the fixed HCU. HybridQC enables designers to study topology, scheduling, and workload growth before tightly integrated quantum-classical machines exist physically.

papers.title: Reasoning about Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) is a computing paradigm in which measurements yield values over a continuous domain. CVQC is both a convenient computational framework for modeling physical quantum systems, and a good abstraction for hardware platforms based on quantum optics. Yet, the semantic foundations of CVQC remain underdeveloped. To address this gap, we develop a formal semantics for a core CV quantum programming language, and sound verification methods for program correctness. A main contribution of this work is to isolate a well-behaved quantitative predicate domain that achieves sufficient expressiveness to accommodate unbounded values as they arise in the infinite-dimensional, continuous setting. Specifically, we choose closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, representing finite expectations, domains of finiteness, and infinite penalties in one ordered object. We validate our choice by establishing that our semantic predicates satisfy desirable closure properties including the definition of weakest preconditions. We validate our design with two case studies, including an example based on the celebrated GKP error-correcting code, for which we establish a second moment bound.

papers.title: Magneto-oscillations, nonlinearity, and nonreciprocity of Coulomb drag in quantum circuits
papers.summary: We consider the problem of Coulomb drag in interactively coupled quantum circuits built of adiabatic constrictions: quantum point contacts and short quantum-wire channels. The interplay of spatial confinement and magnetic field leads to a rich oscillatory response of the drag current as a function of gate voltage and magnetic field: drag peaks track the depopulation of magnetoelectric subbands, are asymptotically periodic in inverse field, and their visibility is controlled by the competition of temperature with the field-sharpened tunneling width of the constriction. We derive a closed expression for the linear drag conductance whose interaction kernel simplifies dramatically in the experimentally relevant limit of a long thermal length compared with the range of the interwire coupling, investigate the drag in the nonlinear regime, where the drag current measures the transconductance of the drive channel at any field, and discuss physically motivated models of dissipation-induced nonreciprocity of the drag signal. Extensions accounting for Zeeman splitting, interaction renormalization of the barrier transmission, backscattering at high field, and the frequency structure of the circuit coupling delineate how each mechanism imprints itself on the temperature dependence and lineshapes of the drag oscillations.

papers.title: Sparse Walsh-Pauli Correlation Encoding for MaxCut: A Quantum-Inspired Formulation with Quantum-Hardware Validation
papers.summary: We introduce a sparse Walsh-Pauli correlation encoding for MaxCut, in which graph variables are represented by diagonal Pauli-string expectation values computed classically as normalized XOR autocorrelations of Walsh coefficients. The complete Walsh basis can reproduce the diagonal correlators of arbitrary quantum states, while a structured sparse support reduces the number of trainable coefficients to $m+1$ for $m$ graph variables. We evaluate the method on $1{,}400$ held-out random graphs with up to $7{,}000$ vertices, obtaining empirical approximation ratios near $0.98$ relative to MQLib heuristic references. On Gset instances G14, G23, G60, and G64, the sparse model achieves mean refined approximation ratios of $0.9828$, $0.9926$, $0.9781$, and $0.9369$, respectively, with $80.4\%$-$89.3\%$ fewer parameters than the complete Walsh representation. The trained coefficients are transferred without retraining to quantum circuits. Statevector simulations of the four Gset instances achieve fidelities above $0.99994$ and preserve all correlator signs. Separately, a seven-qubit experiment on a $15$-vertex graph executed on IBM quantum hardware achieves a correlator-sign agreement of $0.927\pm0.049$ relative to the corresponding noiseless circuit. These results demonstrate the potential of sparse Walsh-PCE for large-instance quantum-inspired MaxCut optimization while validating the transfer of classically trained parameters to quantum hardware.

papers.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
papers.summary: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match: worth only a factor 1.15. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a further 2.7. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV- spin coherence rather than shortening it.

papers.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
papers.summary: We study symmetric gapped ground states of one-dimensional spin $S$ chains with a continuous exponential symmetry $U(1)\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with integer base $q$, where the U(1) charge has a modulated unit of charge $q^{L-j}$ decaying exponentially with site $j$. The simplest model is a quantum breakdown model that can be viewed as a $q$-deformation of the XXZ Haldane spin chain. We show that the topology of their symmetric ground states crucially depends on $S$ and $q$. For integer $S$, odd $q$ allows a nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ Haldane-type symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase with protected edge modes, while even $q$ allows no nontrivial SPT phase. For half-odd integer $S$, odd $q$ prohibits any unique symmetric gapped ground state due to a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis obstruction, whereas even $q$ enforces a novel symmetric gapped phase which we name as the ``half-SPT" phase. Unconventionally, the half-SPT phase only has a symmetry protected edge mode on one edge, and has half of the string orders of an SPT phase. Our results uncover a new type of symmetry-protected gapped phases beyond existing classification schemes.

papers.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
papers.summary: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.

papers.title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
papers.summary: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.

papers.title: Resonant suppression of the $\pi$-type Josephson component in a Kitaev-ladder junction
papers.summary: We investigate Josephson transport through a finite normal segment connecting two Kitaev-ladder superconductors and show that discrete-level detuning controls the sign of the equilibrium Josephson coupling through a branch-selection mechanism. Away from resonance, detuning separates two competing low-energy branches, allowing inter-leg hybridization to clamp the $0$-phase-favoring branch while leaving the $\pi$-favoring branch dispersive. The resulting negative first harmonic evolves from a branch-switching response at weak coupling into a smooth $\pi$-junction regime. At resonance the two clamping thresholds coincide, so the finite interval in which only one branch remains dispersive disappears. Once the inter-leg coupling exceeds the resonant clamping threshold, both low-energy branches become independent of the Josephson phase. The remaining finite-energy states then generate a $0$-type Josephson coupling. At $\phi=\pi$, the helicity decomposition yields an exact clamping identity for arbitrary finite normal-segment length. Within the controlled sweet-point finite-segment theory, serial propagation fixes the off-resonant fourth-order harmonic to be negative, whereas an isolated resonance leaves a positive residual harmonic within the resonant clamping regime. Numerical calculations demonstrate that the resonance-induced suppression persists away from the solvable phase choice. Thus normal-level resonance does not merely enhance Josephson transmission; it changes which low-energy branches contribute to the Josephson coupling.

papers.title: Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite
papers.summary: Herbertsmithite (ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$) is one of the most extensively studied quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidates, yet the precise nature of its ground state remains unresolved. Here, we compare the results of high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of herbertsmithite (Zn$_\mathrm{x}$Cu$_\mathrm{4-x}$(OD)$_6$Cl$_2$, $x\simeq 0.85$) with large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and dynamical DMRG simulations to benchmark the spin Hamiltonian and uncover fundamental properties of the ground state. The measured spin correlations determine an energy density for the Heisenberg model that closely matches simulations, an essential verification of the Hamiltonian. In parallel, DMRG simulations reveal two nearly degenerate QSL states. Both preserve translational symmetry, but one retains the lattice point-group symmetries whereas the other develops anisotropic spin correlations that break point-group symmetry. These two QSLs have distinct spin structure factors, and, remarkably, close agreement with the neutron spectra is achieved with an admixture of the two states. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between neutron scattering and simulations, and suggest that herbertsmithite realizes a regime in which two proximate gapped QSL states coexist.

papers.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
papers.summary: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.

papers.title: Quantifying the Kinetic and Thermodynamic Origins of the Glass-Forming Ability in Metals
papers.summary: The glass-forming ability (GFA) of a metallic liquid can be quantified by the critical cooling rate $R_c$, below which it crystallizes upon cooling. $R_c$ is determined by the competition between $R$ and the crystallization rate $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$. Here, we calculate $R_c$ and $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ in model pure metals and alloys with BCC/B2 and FCC equilibrium crystal structures. Using classical nucleation theory and independently calculated crystal growth rates, we evaluate $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}=(IU^3)^{1/4}$ at $T=0.8T_m$, where $I$ and $U$ are the nucleation and growth rates and $T_m$ is the melting temperature. We find a strong positive correlation between $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ and $R_c$ over eleven orders of magnitude. We decompose $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ into a product of a kinetic contribution, involving atomic cluster attachment and diffusion, and a thermodynamic contribution. We show that the thermodynamic contribution to $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ dominates the kinetic contribution over the range of cooling rates that we consider. The nucleation barrier $\Delta G_c \sim \tilde\gamma^3/\Delta\tilde\mu^2$, where $\tilde\gamma$ is the reduced effective liquid--crystal interfacial free energy and $\Delta\tilde\mu$ is the reduced bulk driving force, determines the magnitude of the thermodynamic contribution. The relative importance of $\tilde\gamma$ and $\Delta\tilde\mu$ depends on the material: a large interfacial free energy can suppress nucleation in some systems, whereas a weak bulk driving force can inhibit crystallization in others. Analyses of the structural and chemical order show that better glass formers have enhanced structural frustration, more icosahedral-like and less crystal-like local environments, and a larger chemical-order mismatch between the supercooled liquid and crystal phases.
