papers.title: From Inference to Control: Structure-Guided Control of Hypergraph Dynamics
papers.summary: Controllability determines whether a system's state can be guided toward any desired configuration, making it a fundamental prerequisite for designing effective control strategies. In the context of networked systems, controllability is a well-established concept. However, many real-world systems, from biological collectives to engineered infrastructures, exhibit higher-order interactions that cannot be captured by simple graphs. Moreover, the interaction structures might be unknown and difficult to measure directly. Here, we close this gap by combining hypergraph inference with the identification of controllable nodes. Building on the inferred structure, we design a controller that, given a set of controllable nodes, steers the system toward a desired configuration. We formulate analytical controllability guarantees for polynomial systems. For non-polynomial dynamics on hypergraphs, we propose a heuristic method for identifying controllable nodes and validate the proposed approach using Kuramoto oscillators.

papers.title: An Exact Solution Algorithm for the Bi-Level Optimization Problem of Electric Vehicles Charging Station Placement
papers.summary: This work addresses electric vehicle (EV) charging station placement through a bi-level optimization model, where the upper-level planner maximizes charging revenue by selecting station locations under budget constraints, while EV users at the lower level choose routes and charging stations to minimize travel and charging costs. To account for battery range limitation, we construct a battery-expanded network and apply a shortest path algorithm with Frank-Wolfe traffic assignment. Our primary contribution is developing the first global solution algorithm for large scale EV charging station placement problems. We propose a Branch-and-Price-and-Cut algorithm enhanced with value function cuts and column generation. Our exact algorithm delivers solutions provably within the reported optimality gap of the global optimum with mathematical certainty. Computational experiments on the Eastern Massachusetts network (74 nodes, 248 links), the Anaheim network (416 nodes, 914 links), and the Barcelona network (110 zones, 1,020 nodes, and 2,512 links) demonstrate exceptional performance. Our algorithm terminates in a reasonable runtime while achieving optimality gaps below 1% across all instances. Controlled benchmarks against two genetic algorithms on identical instances confirm that the proposed algorithm finds equal or better solutions in less computation time across all tested networks. The algorithm successfully handles problems with over 300,000 feasible combinations, transforming EV charging infrastructure planning into a tractable optimization suitable for practical decision making on real-world networks with optimality guaranteed.

papers.title: Braess' Paradoxes in Coupled Power and Transportation Systems
papers.summary: Transportation electrification introduces strong coupling between the power and transportation systems. In this paper, we generalize the classical notion of Braess' paradox to coupled power and transportation systems, and examine how the cross-system coupling induces new types of Braess' paradoxes. To this end, we model the power and transportation networks as graphs, coupled with charging points connecting to nodes in both graphs. The power system operation is characterized by the economic dispatch optimization, while the transportation system user equilibrium models travelers' route and charging choices. By analyzing simple coupled systems, we demonstrate that capacity expansion in either the transportation or the power system can deteriorate the performance of both systems, and uncover the fundamental mechanisms for such new Braess' paradoxes to occur. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the occurrence of Braess' paradoxes in general coupled systems, leading to managerial insights for infrastructure planners. For general networks, by characterizing generalized user equilibria of coupled systems, we develop charging-pricing policies to mitigate Braess' paradoxes.

papers.title: LEO Constellations as a Decentralized GNSS Network: Optimizing PNT Corrections in Space
papers.summary: With the rapid expansion of low Earth orbit (LEO) constellations, thousands of satellites are now in operation, many equipped with onboard GNSS receivers capable of continuous orbit determination and time synchronization. This development is creating an unprecedented spaceborne GNSS network, offering new opportunities for network-driven precise LEO orbit and clock estimation. Yet, current onboard GNSS processing is largely standalone and often insufficient for high-precision applications, while centralized fusion is challenging due to computational bottlenecks and the lack of in-orbit infrastructure. In this work, we report a decentralized GNSS network over large-scale LEO constellations, where each satellite processes its own measurements while exchanging compact information with neighboring nodes to enable precise orbit and time determination. We model the moving constellation as a dynamic graph and employ a momentum-accelerated gradient tracking (GT) method to achieve stable convergence despite topology changes. Numerical simulations with constellations containing hundreds of satellites show that the proposed method matches the accuracy of an ideal centralized benchmark. Ultimately, this framework supports the development of autonomous and self-organizing space systems, enabling high-precision navigation with reduced dependence on continuous ground contact.

papers.title: Diagnostic Impact of Cine Clips for Thyroid Nodule Assessment on Ultrasound
papers.summary: Objective: Thyroid ultrasound is commonly performed using a combination of static images and cine clips (video recordings). However, the exact utility and impact of cine images remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of cine imaging on accuracy and consistency of thyroid nodule assessment, using the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging, Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS). Methods: 50 benign and 50 malignant thyroid nodules with cytopathology results, from 89 patients, were included. A reader study with 4 specialty-trained radiologists was then conducted over 3 rounds, assessing only static images in the first two rounds and both static and cine images in the third round. TI-RADS scores and the consequent management recommendations were then evaluated by comparing them to the malignancy status of the nodules. Results: Mean sensitivity for malignancy detection was 0.65 for static images and 0.67 with both static and cine images (p=0.41). Specificity was 0.20 for static images and 0.22 with both static and cine images (p=0.25). Management recommendations were similar with and without cine images. Intrareader agreement on feature assignments was slightly lower when cine images were added (0.83 vs 0.87, p<0.001), and TI-RADS point totals changed more between rounds with cine images. Conclusion: The inclusion of cine imaging for thyroid nodule assessment on ultrasound did not significantly change diagnostic performance in this reader study, although it changed some feature assignments. Current practice guidelines, which do not mandate cine imaging, may be sufficient for TI-RADS-based management recommendations.

papers.title: Robust Hybrid Finite-Time Parameter Estimation Without Persistence of Excitation
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating parameters of a linear regression model. Using a hybrid systems framework, a hybrid algorithm is proposed allowing the estimate to converge to the exact value of the unknown parameters in predetermined finite time. Interestingly, we show that for the case of constant parameters, the convergence property of the hybrid algorithm holds while only requiring the regressor to be exciting on a given interval. For the case of piecewise constant parameters, the classical persistency of excitation condition is required to guarantee the convergence. Robustness of the proposed algorithm with respect to measurements noise is analysed. Finally, illustrative examples are provided showing the merits of the proposed approach in terms of scalability and the applicability for the general class of time-varying unknown parameters

papers.title: Stable Inversion of Discrete-Time Linear Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation
papers.summary: Inverse systems for discrete-time linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants are fundamental to feedforward control and iterative learning control of multirate and periodic systems. Building on the classical cyclic reformulation, which converts an N-periodic system into an equivalent LTI system at the original sampling rate, this paper derives an explicit closed-form N-periodic state-space realization of the inverse for an arbitrary uniform periodic relative degree r >= 0 (defined through the periodic Markov parameters). The technical basis is a structure-preservation property: after absorbing a phase shift for r >= 1, the LTI inverse of the cycled plant provably retains the cyclic (block-circulant/block-diagonal) structure, so that the periodic inverse matrices can be read off block-by-block, in exact correspondence with the LTI inverse. The resulting inverse system is real-valued, causal for r = 0 and r-step-delayed for r >= 1, operates at the original sampling rate, and reconstructs the input exactly under matched initial conditions, with geometric error decay otherwise. Through this correspondence, its stability is shown to be equivalent to the invariant zeros of the cycled plant - the periodic invariant zeros of the plant - lying in the open unit disk, which generalizes the minimum phase condition of the LTI case and is verifiable on a single constant matrix pencil. Numerical examples illustrate the construction, the stability characterization, and the implementation as an online periodic filter.

papers.title: Joint Training Scattering Matrix Learning and Channel Estimation for Beyond-Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
papers.summary: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) generalizes the conventional diagonal RIS (D-RIS) by introducing tunable inter-element connections, offering enhanced wave manipulation capabilities. However, realizing the advantages of BD-RIS requires accurate channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition becomes significantly more challenging due to the increased number of channel coefficients, leading to prohibitively large pilot training overhead in BD-RIS-aided multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Existing studies reduce pilot overhead by exploiting the channel correlations induced by the Kronecker-product or multi-linear structure of BD-RIS-aided channels, which neglect the spatial correlation among antennas and the statistical correlation across RIS-user channels. In this paper, we propose a learning-based channel estimation framework, namely the joint training scattering matrix learning and channel estimation framework (JTSMLCEF), which jointly optimizes the BD-RIS training scattering matrix and estimates the cascaded channels in an end-to-end manner to achieve accurate channel estimation and reduce the pilot overhead. The proposed JTSMLCEF follows a two-phase channel estimation protocol to enable adaptive training scattering matrix optimization with a training scattering matrix optimizer (TSMO) and cascaded channel estimation with a dual-attention channel estimator (DACE). Specifically, the DACE is designed with intra-user and inter-user attention modules to capture the multi-dimensional correlations in multi-user cascaded channels. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of JTSMLCEF. Compared with the current state-of-the-art method, it reduces the pilot overhead by $80\%$ while further reducing the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) by $82.6\%$ and $92.5\%$ in indoor and urban micro-cell (UMi) scenarios, respectively.

papers.title: Beyond the Flat-Spike: Adaptive Sparse CCA for Decaying and Unbalanced Signals
papers.summary: Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SCCA) is a fundamental statistical tool for identifying linear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-view data. While minimax theory establishes an optimal sample complexity scaling additively with the sparsity levels of the canonical vectors, computationally efficient algorithms typically suffer from a suboptimal multiplicative dependence. This computational-statistical gap is intrinsically tied to worst-case ``flat'' signal assumptions. In practice, however, multi-view signals frequently exhibit structured energy concentration, such as a power-law decay. To exploit this structural concentration and bypass the worst-case bottleneck, we propose Bilateral Spectral Energy Pursuit (Bi-SEP). Operating directly on the cross-covariance matrix, Bi-SEP is a stagewise adaptive algorithm that utilizes a proxy refinement step to dynamically track and capture cross-view signal energy. Theoretically, we establish a profile-adaptive sample complexity bound governed by the coupled energy profiles of the two views. Notably, under power-law decay models, we reveal a synergistic phase transition: the optimal linear sample complexity is attainable provided that the aggregate decay rate of the two views is sufficiently large. This result demonstrates that a highly concentrated signal in one view allows the model to accommodate a completely flat signal in its partner. Numerical experiments validate our theoretical findings, illustrating the advantages of Bi-SEP in structured, non-flat signal regimes.

papers.title: Dynamic Quantum-Assisted Co-Design of Controller and Lyapunov Candidate Parameters for Nonlinear Systems
papers.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic quantum-assisted co-design framework for nonlinear closed-loop systems in which controller parameters and Lyapunov candidate parameters are redesigned jointly at successive decision epochs. Unlike conventional nonlinear control designs that typically tune controller gains offline and perform stability analysis separately, the proposed method embeds performance improvement and sample-based Lyapunov verification within a unified online optimization loop. The main novelty is a two-step computational structure that first contracts the continuous admissible search region around the current operating condition using a Black-Hole calibration procedure and then constructs a finite binary representation only over this calibrated region. The encoded objective is obtained from sampled nonlinear closed-loop evaluations and approximated by a local quadratic pseudo-Boolean surrogate, enabling an Ising-type Hamiltonian representation suitable for quantum-assisted optimization. Quantum imaginary time evolution is then used to explore the encoded Hamiltonian, and the resulting candidate bitstrings are decoded into continuous controller and Lyapunov parameters. To reduce dependence on the surrogate model, the decoded candidates are re-evaluated using the original nonlinear closed-loop cost and Lyapunov penalties before the final update is applied. The framework can accommodate sampled forms of different Lyapunov decay specifications by modifying the corresponding penalty and is numerically evaluated on first-order nonlinear consensus, second-order nonlinear consensus, and induction motor drive control examples. The implementation code used to generate the reported results is available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DQCLS-NS}{GitHub}.

papers.title: Coupling-Aware Pinching-Antenna Radiation for Heterogeneous NOMA Users
papers.summary: Pinching-antennas systems (PASS) offer reconfigurable wireless channels via low-cost dielectric mediums by creating line-of-sight (LoS) communication links. Most of the existing PASS cover mechanisms of equal power pinching antennas for conventional bit-based communication, whereas flexible radiation control remains largely unexplored, particularly for heterogeneous semantic and bit users. In this paper, we investigate the performance of semantic communication (SC) using an adjustable radiation model over PASS, where the coupling strength between the dielectric waveguide and each pinching antenna is determined by the antenna-waveguide spacing. Specifically, the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted heterogeneous users are served by multiple pinching antennas using spacing-controlled adjustable radiation ratios. Uunder this setting, we maximize the semantic spectral efficiency (SE) subject to the bit-user quality of service (QoS) requirement, successive interference cancellation (SIC) feasibility, and the minimum adjacent antennas spacing constraint. An alternating optimization (AO) approach optimizes users power allocation and positions of pinching antennas. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proportional power PASS model in providing higher semantic SE in different geometrical and numerical settings compared to conventional benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Domain-Agnostic Incremental Learning for Sound Classification. A DCASE 2026 Challenge task
papers.summary: This paper presents the Domain-Agnostic Incremental Learning for Audio Classification Task of the DCASE 2026 Challenge. Incremental learning refers to sequentially learning new tasks with the same system while maintaining its knowledge and performance on the previously learned task. Domain-incremental learning for sound classification refers to learning the same sound classes but in different acoustic domains, and was formalized as a data challenge for the first time in DCASE 2026. The task required participants to train a system to learn ten sound classes in three different domains, starting from a baseline system trained on the first domain. At each incremental task, learning had to be done without access to previous task data. The systems were ranked by the overall average accuracy calculated over the three domains. The task generated high interest and received submissions from 21 teams, with most submissions outperforming the provided baseline system. The highest performance of 79.6% was obtained using a combination of continual learning strategies that resulted in a balanced accuracy across domains, hence a good balance of retaining old and learning new information.

papers.title: Interpreting Content and Speaker Characteristics in Factorised Self-Supervised Subspaces
papers.summary: Self-supervised speech features encode both content and speaker information. Recent work introduced an SVD-based factorisation method that decomposes these features into a shared content matrix capturing temporal variation and speaker-specific transformations capturing static speaker characteristics. However, how information is organised within these components remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate how the dimensions of WavLM-factorised content and speaker subspaces correlate with speech characteristics such as pitch, intensity, and voicing. We find that leading dimensions in the content space primarily capture intensity, higher-order formants, and voicing, while pitch is encoded in a later dimension. In contrast, the highest-variance speaker dimension is strongly associated with pitch and gender, with later dimensions capturing high-frequency variation. Intervention experiments show that manipulating these dimensions enables targeted control of speech characteristics for speech synthesis. Furthermore, modifying the content and speaker representations jointly provides fine-grained control over characteristics such as pitch and intensity.

papers.title: Cyclic Reformulation-Based Identification and Polytopic Uncertainty Modeling for Multirate Systems
papers.summary: Modern control systems increasingly rely on heterogeneous sensors operating at different sampling rates, where intermittently missing outputs pose fundamental challenges for system identification. This paper proposes a non-iterative, control-oriented identification method for multirate systems based on cyclic reformulation. The method transforms multirate data into an expanded time-invariant representation and yields M parameter sets from a single input-output dataset, where M is the least common multiple of the sensor sampling periods. These parameter sets, expressed in a common state coordinate of the original dimension, are used in two complementary ways: their centroid, in which each output row is averaged over the phases at which that output is observed, serves as a noise-reduced nominal model, while their convex hull gives a polytopic uncertainty model whose vertices can be used directly in vertex-based LMI robust control design. Building on the exact cyclic-structure recovery established in the authors' preceding work, the paper contributes the centroid and polytopic models and evaluates them under finite noise through output-level validation statistics. Numerical simulations support both models: an illustrative SISO example shows that the centroid attains higher validation FIT than the best individual vertex and substantially outperforms an interpolation-based baseline, while a MIMO multirate sensing example confirms that the constructed polytope contains models whose validation FIT exceeds 95% on average even at the highest tested noise level. The resulting polytope is a data-derived uncertainty description obtained from a single experiment, so that the framework links multirate system identification with robust-control-oriented uncertainty modeling without iterative EM-type optimization.

papers.title: WULPUS PRO: Multi-mode Ultra-Low-Power Wearable Ultrasound and Array Imaging with CMUT Support
papers.summary: Wearable ultrasound enables continuous monitoring of physiological processes such as muscle dynamics, bladder volume, and cardiovascular activity. Existing fully wearable ultra-low-power platforms are limited to shallow, low-channel A-mode sensing, while larger multi-mode systems are too bulky and power-hungry for true wearability. We present WULPUS PRO, a runtime-programmable wearable ultrasound acquisition platform measuring $39\times21\times6 \mathrm{mm}$ and weighing $5 \mathrm{g}$. It integrates $30 \mathrm{V}$ excitation, 16 time-multiplexed channels, a low-noise receive front-end with up to $70 \mathrm{dB}$ gain, $14 \mathrm{MHz}$ bandwidth, time-gain compensation, and $45 \mathrm{dB}$ SNR. The platform supports deep-tissue echo acquisition up to $2.2 \mathrm{MHz}$ in RF-sampling mode and $8 \mathrm{MHz}$ in envelope-detection mode. We demonstrate B-mode imaging in a 16-channel ultra-low-power wearable with sub-millimeter axial and millimeter-scale lateral resolution in phantom experiments, while consuming $40 \mathrm{mW}$ at $50 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF and under $60 \mathrm{mW}$ at $300 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF. WULPUS PRO supports both piezoelectric and capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducers, enabling integration with skin-conformal polymer-based CMUT arrays. As a host-agnostic acquisition front-end, it exposes standard data and power interfaces for BLE- and Wi-Fi-based wearable hosts. We demonstrate wireless transmission with external BLE and Wi-Fi modules and project 1-2 days of BLE operation at $50 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF and over 3 h of Wi-Fi streaming at $300 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF using a $300 \mathrm{mAh}$, $6.4 \mathrm{g}$ Li-Po cell. WULPUS PRO establishes a new class of fully programmable, B-mode-enabled, ultra-low-power wearable ultrasound platforms.

papers.title: Dynamic Constraint Reconstruction Based Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Critical Control of High-Dimensional Manipulators
papers.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for constrained nonlinear systems, but their effectiveness relies on accurate system dynamics. In high-dimensional manipulators subject to unknown disturbances and model uncertainties, fixed safety constraints constructed from nominal dynamics may become inconsistent with the actual system behavior, leading to safety degradation or excessive conservatism. This paper proposes a dynamic constraint reconstruction based control barrier function (DCR-CBF) framework for safety-critical control of disturbed robotic manipulators. An extended state observer is employed to estimate lumped disturbances online, and the estimated disturbance is incorporated into high-order control barrier functions to reconstruct safety constraints according to the estimated true dynamics. To address estimation inaccuracies, a safety margin is introduced, and a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee forward invariance under bounded estimation errors. Simulation studies on a 4-DOF excavation manipulator demonstrate that the proposed DCR-CBF method achieves zero safety violation under strong unknown disturbances while significantly improving trajectory-tracking performance compared with standard and robust CBF methods.

papers.title: On the Detection Optimality and Exact BER Analysis of NOMA
papers.summary: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) detection using successive interference cancellation (SIC) and joint multiuser maximum likelihood (JML) has been extensively studied, although their presumed optimality for individual-user bit error rate (BER) minimization is unestablished. Moreover, existing BER analyses overlook the SIC-induced statistical changes. This letter derives optimal per-user maximum a posteriori (MAP) detectors, identifies when the near-user detector reduces to conventional SIC, and proves the equivalence of conventional SIC and JML. An exact average BER analysis accounting for SIC-induced statistical changes is presented. The results show that the proposed detector achieves modest but consistent BER gains at low-to-moderate signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

papers.title: Age-of-Information Aware Federated Learning with Finite Speed Pinching Antenna
papers.summary: This paper investigates age-of-information (AoI) aware federated learning over wireless networks with finite speed pinching antennas. In contrast to existing studies that assume an infinitely high antenna moving speed, a practical round based training procedure is considered, where the pinching antenna is repositioned during the local training phase and its feasible movement range depends on the selected devices. This creates a new coupling among device selection, antenna placement, local training time, model uploading time, and AoI evolution. To characterize the impact of antenna moving speed, the rate gain over the fixed antenna and the gap to the infinite speed benchmark are analyzed. Subsequently, an overall AoI minimization problem is formulated under a round latency deadline by jointly optimizing the selected device set and the pinching antenna position. A coalitional game based device selection algorithm is proposed, where finite speed antenna placement is incorporated into the coalition utility evaluation. For antenna placement, the optimal search region is derived by exploiting the mobility constraint and device location span, based on which a branch-and-bound (BnB) algorithm is developed to obtain the global optimum. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can accelerate learning convergence, reduce the sum AoI, and improve device participation compared with baseline schemes, demonstrating the potential of pinching antennas for enhancing federated learning through flexible spatial reconfiguration.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Optimisation Framework for Integrated Electric-Hydrogen-Transport Systems
papers.summary: Integrated electric-hydrogen infrastructures are becoming increasingly important with the growing deployment of electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen vehicles (HVs) in transport systems. However, the strong coupling between vehicle scheduling and multi-energy dispatch introduces significant operational challenges. This paper models an integrated electric-hydrogen-transport system (EHTS) and proposes a hierarchical optimisation framework that couples vehicle scheduling and downstream energy dispatch through a sequential, demand-driven two-layer structure. In the vehicle scheduling layer, a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) algorithm is developed to avoid repeated optimisation solving, enabling real-time EV charging and HV refuelling under non-preemptive service and within-interval sequential assignment. The resulting charging and refuelling demands are subsequently passed to the energy dispatch layer, where a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based approach is designed to optimise battery operation, hydrogen-tank operation, and PV generation allocation to minimise the overall operational cost of the EHTS while satisfying the scheduled transport demand. Representative case studies, together with comparative, ablation, and generalisation analyses, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. Furthermore, the learned dispatch policy maintains strong performance across diverse transport-demand scenarios and PV penetration levels without retraining, demonstrating robust generalisation capability for practical deployment.

papers.title: Analytical Prediction of Voltage Collapse in Current-Limited Grid-Forming Inverters
papers.summary: As converter-interfaced units become dominant in power systems, understanding nonlinear stability phenomena involving discrete switching events becomes essential for secure operation. The limited overcurrent capability of grid-forming (GFM) inverters makes current limiting essential during large disturbances. Activation of a circular current limiter (CCL) can cause the operating equilibrium to disappear under certain circumstances. This paper develops an analytical framework to predict the grid-voltage boundaries for CCL activation and determine whether the operating equilibrium persists or disappears after activation. For CCL-based GFM inverters with frozen anti-windup, closed-form expressions for the activation boundaries are derived while accounting for the filter capacitor. A criterion is established to determine whether a saturated (i.e., current-limited) stable equilibrium point (satSEP) persists following limiter activation. A continuation method is also developed to trace equilibria across normal-control and current-limited operation. Power-angle analysis and dynamic-model continuation in single-inverter and modified 9-bus systems validate these predictions. Time-domain simulations further confirm the results. The results show that CCL activation can either cause immediate loss of the stable equilibrium or allow stable current-limited operation to continue until the equilibrium is lost as operating conditions change further.

papers.title: Reduced Arc-Weight Heterogeneity for Master Stability Analysis of Directed Networks
papers.summary: Master stability analysis can be applied to directed networks even when their Laplacian matrices are not diagonalizable. Nevertheless, a diagonalizable Laplacian is easier to analyse because the perturbations governing synchronization separate into independent modes. This paper asks how many different positive coupling strengths are needed to obtain this simplification without adding or removing any directed connections. We first give an elementary construction showing that suitable positive weights exist for every weakly connected directed network and explain its relationship to stronger genericity results in the literature. We then introduce a measure of the smallest number of distinct coupling strengths required for diagonalizability. If a common coupling strength already produces a diagonalizable Laplacian, only one value is needed. For directed acyclic networks, we give a constructive upper bound based on the length of the longest directed path from a source. This bound is exact for rooted outward directed trees. Consequently, an outward star requires only one coupling value, whereas a directed path requires a different value on every arc. These results reduce coupling heterogeneity while retaining the simpler modal form of master stability analysis. Diagonalizability is treated as an analytical convenience, not as a sufficient condition for synchronization.

papers.title: A Control Co-Design Framework to Optimize Sustainability with Application to Microgrid-Driven Data Centers
papers.summary: This work studies the optimization of physical plant characteristics and controller parameters for sustainability. Environmental sustainability is strongly correlated with the development and operation of energy systems, with data centers as the preeminent modern example. Data centers, and the grid technologies that provide their power, consume nonnegligible amounts of global energy and pose a risk to increase greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and electronic waste. Addressing such issues requires improved plant design and control strategies, often approached through optimization-based methods. However, there are noticeable gaps regarding data center and microgrid design: (i) simultaneous optimization of plant and controller features is rarely explored, and (ii) sustainability criteria are not emphasized. This work addresses these gaps by establishing a generalized, sustainability-centric control co-design (CCD) framework for energy systems. Uniquely, the CCD framework defines and categorizes sustainability metrics into three lifecycle stages - manufacturing, operation, and disposal - supporting optimization and comparative analysis of the metrics for different design options. To exemplify its use, the CCD framework is applied to a microgrid-driven data center system, providing a family of sustainability metrics correlated to plant and controller parameters. The analysis enabled by the framework supports the determination of tradeoffs between different types of environmental sustainability metrics. The system designs identified by the proposed framework show substantial improvements to environmental sustainability categories as compared to designs identified through baseline procedures.

papers.title: Joint Beamforming Optimization and Dynamic Tracking in RIS-Enabled Secure ISAC Systems
papers.summary: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the direct links between the base station (BS) and users are blocked, and the mobile eavesdropper is treated as the sensing target. The mobility of the eavesdropper induces time-varying wiretap channels, potentially compromising secure transmission when outdated eavesdropper information is used. To address this challenge, the BS dynamically tracks the eavesdropper over consecutive time slots and exploits the predicted state information to adapt its transmission strategy. A sum secrecy rate maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the BS beamforming, artificial noise, and RIS reflection coefficients, subject to a constraint on the tracking error covariance to ensure the required sensing accuracy. To tackle the resulting nonconvex optimization problem with temporal coupling, an iterative algorithm integrating an extended Kalman filter (EKF) with an alternating optimization framework is developed. Specifically, the EKF recursively predicts and updates the eavesdropper's state, while the joint optimization problem is decomposed into four tractable subproblems that are solved iteratively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves improved secrecy performance while effectively tracking the trajectory of the mobile eavesdropper, compared with benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Leveraging Movable-Element STARS for RSMA-SWIPT Under Practical System Imperfections
papers.summary: We study a robust multiuser framework for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), where rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) is integrated with a movable-element simultaneously transmitting and reflecting surface (ME-STARS). By allowing the STARS elements to change their positions in addition to controlling the reflection and transmission coefficients, the proposed architecture provides additional spatial flexibility for improving the cascaded channels toward users in both regions. Meanwhile, RSMA is employed to manage multiuser interference, while power-splitting receivers enable simultaneous information decoding and energy harvesting. The system design further accounts for channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, residual transceiver hardware impairments (HIs), and the nonlinear characteristics of practical energy-harvesting circuits. Accordingly, a robust sum-rate maximization problem is formulated by jointly designing the BS precoders, common-rate allocation, ME-STARS reflection/transmission coefficients, power-splitting (PS) ratios, and movable-element positions. The resulting formulation is highly non-convex because the movable-element positions affect the cascaded channels non-linearly and are tightly coupled with the remaining design variables. To obtain a tractable solution, the joint design is decomposed into active beamforming, passive beamforming, movable-element positioning, and PS-ratio optimization blocks, which are updated iteratively through suitable convex reformulations. Numerical results show that the proposed framework delivers higher sum rates than the considered benchmark schemes, exhibits robust behavior under CSI uncertainty and residual HIs, and achieves stable convergence across the considered system configurations.

papers.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
papers.summary: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.

papers.title: Identifiability-Guided Composite Load Modeling of AI Data Centers
papers.summary: The rapid growth of AI data centers introduces large, workload-dependent loads whose protection and reconnection behavior can affect power-system transient stability. Calibrating dynamic models of such loads is challenging because treating all associated elements as freely estimable may lead to weakly identified or physically confounded parameterizations. This paper proposes an identifiability-guided calibration framework for a composite load model with separate IT, cooling, and auxiliary branches. A nuisance-projected Fisher-information criterion characterizes the local identifiability of the cooling-motor composition, while a workload non-equivalence result shows that voltage-only recalibration cannot reproduce workload-dependent responses. Guided by these results, a grey-box estimator trained with branch-level supervision learns the workload-to-power relation and the cooling composition, while retaining a prescribed UPS protection law and an externally anchored reconnect-ramp duration. The learned workload relation is then distilled into a closed form for transient-stability simulation. Evaluation using 300,000 MIT Supercloud GPU power-utilization samples and 12,600 IEEE 39-bus fault scenarios yields an aggregate active-power $R^2$ of 0.948, compared with 0.856 for an LSTM baseline. Removing branch-level supervision preserves relatively high aggregate accuracy but substantially degrades cooling-component recovery. Under unseen deep voltage sags, the proposed model achieves a transient $R^2$ of 0.750, compared with 0.033 for the LSTM. Closed-loop simulations further show that cooling composition and protection behavior can affect retained-load states and voltage responses near protection thresholds.

papers.title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
papers.summary: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

papers.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems
papers.summary: Multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) realizes concurrent acoustic communication and localization, yet the frequency selectivity of the acoustic channel creates uneven positioning capabilities across subcarriers. This paper proposes a localization-oriented subcarrier and power allocation scheme for multi-anchor underwater ISAC systems. We build a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derive closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) under frequency-selective channels with colored noise. We derive a subcarrier-level localization information contribution from the time of arrival Fisher information, which enables localization-oriented resource allocation. We derive several theoretical properties regarding the distance and frequency dependence of the localization information metric, and establish a distance-frequency matching principle. These results provide a theoretical foundation for localization-oriented resource allocation and guide the design of a low-complexity greedy algorithm that improves positioning accuracy. Specifically, the algorithm iteratively allocates subcarriers to minimize the residual positioning-error objective, thereby improving positioning accuracy while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Simulations verify that our method yields much lower positioning error bound than uniform, random and high-frequency-first subcarrier allocation in symmetric or asymmetric topologies while guaranteeing communication QoS, achieving superior communication-localization tradeoffs.

papers.title: Topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems
papers.summary: We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.

papers.title: FairShare: Auditable Geographic Fairness for Multi-Operator LEO Spectrum Sharing
papers.summary: Dynamic spectrum sharing (DSS) among multi-operator low Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations is essential for coexistence, yet prevailing policies focus almost exclusively on interference mitigation, leaving geographic equity largely unaddressed. This work investigates whether conventional DSS approaches inadvertently exacerbate the rural digital divide. Incorporating Keplerian orbital dynamics, inter-beam co-channel interference, and three real-world constellation geometries (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), we conduct large-scale, 3GPP-compliant non-terrestrial network (NTN) simulations across 20 orbital snapshots spanning 10~minutes of satellite motion. The results uncover a stark and persistent structural bias: SNR-priority scheduling induces a $1.84\times$ mean urban--rural access disparity, with temporal fluctuations reaching $3.9\times$ during favorable interference conditions. Counter-intuitively, increasing system bandwidth amplifies rather than alleviates this gap. To remedy this, we propose FairShare, a lightweight, quota-based framework that enforces geographic fairness. FairShare not only reverses the bias, achieving an affirmative disparity ratio of $\Delta_{\text{geo}} = 0.68\times$ with zero variance across all orbital snapshots and interference conditions, but also reduces scheduler runtime by 3.3\%. This demonstrates that algorithmic fairness can be achieved without trading off efficiency or complexity, and that it remains invariant to physical-layer dynamics. Our work provides regulators with both a diagnostic metric for auditing fairness and a practical, enforceable mechanism for equitable spectrum governance in next-generation satellite networks.

papers.title: When is cumulative dose response monotonic? Analysis of incoherent feedforward motifs
papers.summary: We study the monotonicity of the cumulative dose response (cDR) for a class of incoherent feedforward motifs (IFFM) systems with linear intermediate dynamics and nonlinear output dynamics. While the instantaneous dose response (DR) may be nonmonotone with respect to the input, the cDR can still be monotone. To analyze this phenomenon, we derive an integral representation of the sensitivity of cDR with respect to the input and establish general sufficient conditions for both monotonicity and nonmonotonicity. These results reduce the problem to verifying qualitative sign properties along system trajectories. The structural conditions identify eight canonical IFFM models, four of which are analyzed in detail within the proposed framework. In particular, IFFM1 and IFFM3 exhibit monotone cDR despite potentially nonmonotone DR, while IFFM2 is monotone already at the level of DR, which implies monotonicity of cDR. In contrast, IFFM4 exhibits nonmonotone cDR. Numerical simulations indicate that these properties persist beyond the structured initial conditions used in the analysis. Overall, our results provide a unified framework for understanding how system structure shapes monotonicity in cumulative input--output responses.

papers.title: Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Nonlinear Control
papers.summary: We study finite-horizon rate-cost tradeoffs for general stochastic control systems, including nonlinear systems. Under an average control cost constraint, we show that the minimum expected communication rate lies within an additive logarithmic gap above the normalized directed information minimized over causal control policies. This establishes directed information as the operationally relevant quantity governing rate-limited control, extending its previously established roles in causal source coding and linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control to general nonlinear control systems.

papers.title: MIRA: A Modular Open-Source Micro-UAV for Indoor Research
papers.summary: Indoor robotics research increasingly relies on micro-UAV platforms whose airframes, electronics, and control software are open to modification. Off-the-shelf platforms often lack the low-level access that such modifications require, while building a custom vehicle demands substantial engineering effort before the first flight test, leaving many laboratories working within constraints that limit the scope of their research. We present MIRA (Modular Indoor Research Architecture), an open-source micro-UAV for indoor research, built around a replicable 3D-printed PLA airframe with detachable arms and a containerized low-level software package that manages the companion-to-autopilot communication bridge via Micro XRCE-DDS. Designed as a white-box architecture, its core subsystems, including the companion computer, are individually replaceable without firmware refactoring, which supports local fabrication, crash-localized repair, and component substitution from existing laboratory inventory. We characterize MIRA through autonomous flights comprising takeoff, hovering, trajectory tracking, and landing within an optical motion-capture volume. The communication pipeline sustains a median companion-to-autopilot latency of 0.02 ms, with the external motion-capture link as the main remaining latency source, and time-domain analysis shows that structural vibration remains stable during dynamic maneuvers and below the reference level adopted in this work. All design files and software are released openly to support replication and extension by other laboratories.

papers.title: Mode-Weighted Transport Certificates for State-Dependent Reflected Switching Diffusions
papers.summary: State-dependent switching diffusions can contract in law even when individual modes are expansive. We establish a computable, constant-one contraction certificate on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and compact convex domains with normal reflection. The mode-weighted transport cost combines spatial separation with a discrete graph penalty and retains spatial dependence when the modes differ. A synchronous Brownian coupling and a maximal coupling of jump clocks in equal modes lead to separate equal- and unequal-mode generator inequalities. We give a complete regularization argument for the nonsmooth cost, including the drift and jump errors, the sign of reflection, and the limiting It\^o-Dynkin calculation. A resolvent proof transfers contraction to probability-valued weak solutions of the no-flux Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov system, while an explicit Foster-Lyapunov condition ensures existence and uniqueness of an invariant law on the whole space. For fixed weight ordering and decay rate, certificate synthesis is a semi-infinite linear feasibility problem; on compact domains, a Lipschitz-buffered finite mesh provides a rigorous test. One-dimensional and planar examples illustrate the certificate and its numerical verification.

papers.title: RDSE: Real-Time Directional Speech Enhancement Framework for Dual-Mic Commodity Smartphones
papers.summary: Audio-visual zooming on mobile devices is fundamentally constrained by limited microphone count, compute resource, unknown array geometry, and weak assumptions on real-world acoustic conditions. We present RDSE: Real-Time Directional Speech Enhancement Framework, a hybrid pipeline that combines traditional signal processing and modern machine learning methods for dual-microphone low-end smartphones. Unlike tightly coupled AV systems that continuously use visual feeds or embeddings, RDSE decouples visual interaction from feature inference, using camera input solely to parameterize the steering vector for spatial filtering. The proposed system uses four modules: dereverberation network, a beamformer with a temporal convolutional network, and a MetricGAN based denoiser. Extensive evaluation on benchmark data and real-world recordings demonstrates effective zooming without precise geometry calibration. Comparative experiments show competitive performance to existing methods. Proposed system is rigorously tested for statistical validity, ablation study, latency profiling, and practicality through real-time live-streaming.

papers.title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion
papers.summary: Safe autonomous navigation using monocular vision remains challenging because explicit obstacle states are not directly observable. This letter introduces a visual safety-certification paradigm that uses scale-free, depth-normalized relative motion encoded by monocular optical flow as the representation for collision-risk certification, without reconstructing obstacle position, velocity, geometry, or a metric world model. Unlike conventional optical-flow-based navigation approaches that rely on image motion to shape avoidance behavior, the proposed framework directly encodes collision-cone geometry and safety constraints in this relative-motion representation. An online Concurrent Learning observer estimates the normalized relative velocity and provides a computable estimation-error bound. This uncertainty is propagated into the collision cone through angular inflation and a monocular robot-footprint margin, yielding a Robust Vision-Based Collision Cone Control Barrier Function (RV-C$^3$BF). An optimal-decay CBF quadratic program minimally modifies the nominal control input to enforce the resulting robust safety constraint under the stated assumptions. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments on a TurtleBot3 in cluttered environments with static and dynamic obstacles demonstrate collision avoidance using only monocular vision and onboard proprioception, with the estimation-error bound containing the measured error in $98.3\%$ of simulation samples and the robot achieving collision-free navigation in $93$ of $100$ real-world trials.
